summary: MarediModa returns to Cannes from 27-29 October 2026, bringing together leading European manufacturers of fabrics and accessories for beachwear, underwear and athleisure. The 24th edition of the international trade fair will take place at the Palais des Festivals, presenting more than 100 collections for the Spring/Summer 2028 season. content: MarediModa returns to Cannes from 27-29 October 2026, bringing together leading European manufacturers of fabrics and accessories for beachwear, underwear and athleisure. The 24th edition of the international trade fair will take place at the Palais des Festivals, presenting more than 100 collections for the Spring/Summer 2028 season. Following earlier events in Miami and Milan, the Cannes exhibition will offer a comprehensive overview of European textile innovation, with a particular emphasis on quality, creativity, ethical manufacturing and environmental responsibility. The programme includes trend presentations, workshops, dedicated athleisure displays, specialist print and design studios, and contract manufacturers, reinforcing MarediModa’s position as a key sourcing event for the premium swimwear, intimate apparel and performancewear sectors. “We return to Cannes following our initiatives in Miami and Milan, confident that we have prepared the year’s key industry event to the highest possible standard,” said Claudio Taiana, President of MarediModa. “In a climate of widespread and profound uncertainty, MarediModa represents a safe harbour in terms of product quality, ethics, innovation and creativity.” A central feature will be the Spring/Summer 2028 trend programme curated by David Shah and his team. Five creative directions will explore changing consumer attitudes, lifestyles, colours and materials across beachwear, bodywear and athleisure. Under the overarching concept Ocean Vibes, the forecasts draw inspiration from music and contemporary subcultures, reflecting a growing emphasis on individuality, optimism and personal expression. title: Archroma Presents Smarter Choices for Competitiveness at Performance Days
summary: Archroma, a global leader in specialty chemicals, will showcase its SUPER SYSTEMS approach to enhancing mill and brand competitiveness at PERFORMANCE DAYS in Munich this week. Drawing on the industry’s most extensive product portfolio and decades of specialized knowledge, SUPER SYSTEMS offers a range of solutions for specific end-uses. Each is calibrated differently across cost […] The post Archroma Presents Smarter Choices for Competitiveness at Performance Days appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Archroma, a global leader in specialty chemicals, will showcase its SUPER SYSTEMS approach to enhancing mill and brand competitiveness at PERFORMANCE DAYS in Munich this week. Drawing on the industry’s most extensive product portfolio and decades of specialized knowledge, SUPER SYSTEMS offers a range of solutions for specific end-uses. Each is calibrated differently across cost efficiency, consumer-driven performance and compliance, so customers across sportswear, outdoor apparel, athleisure and workwear can choose what best fits their strategy. Visitors will also be able to explore individual SUPER SYSTEMS components, such as the industry’s first truly durable silicone softener; performance-assurance programs covering color, UV and water resistance; and biobased innovations spanning gentle cotton preparation, dyes made from wool waste, and plant-based water repellent technologies. “Competitiveness in today’s textile industry is no longer driven by performance, cost or compliance alone. The real challenge is finding the right balance between all three,” said Chiara Galimberti, Brand Engagement, EMEA, Archroma. “At PERFORMANCE DAYS, our specialists can help you identify the combination of solutions that best supports your business priorities.” SUPER SYSTEMS: Empowering a Better Tomorrow Archroma’s SUPER SYSTEMS is a set of end-use focused, fiber-specific solution platforms that require no additional capital investment and work seamlessly from pretreatment to finishing. Each platform combines processing solutions and functional effects with application know-how to help mills and brands improve profitability – through lower total cost in use, premiumization via distinctive coloration and effects, and chemistry that goes beyond compliance to stay ahead of the curve. title: Garment workers’ Tk 30,000 minimum wage demand mounts pressure on RMG, raises ‘Fair Price’ question
summary: Garment workers continued their protests in Uttara and surrounding industrial areas of the capital on Thursday, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000. Workers from several factories took to th...
content: Garment workers continued their protests in Uttara and surrounding industrial areas of the capital on Thursday, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000. Workers from several factories took to the streets and staged blockades, disrupting traffic in parts of the area for a second consecutive day. Workers say rising costs of food, housing, healthcare, education and transportation have made it increasingly difficult to manage household expenses with existing wages. The sustained increase in living costs has therefore renewed demands for a revision of the sector’s minimum wage. Figure: Workers from several factories took to the streets and staged blockades, disrupting traffic in parts of the area for a second consecutive day. In 2023, the minimum monthly wage for Bangladesh’s ready-made garment sector was set at Tk 12,500. Later, the annual wage increment rate was raised from 5 percent to 9 percent in response to inflationary pressure. However, several labor groups argue that the adjustment remains inadequate under current market conditions. While workers are pressing for higher wages, the apparel industry is also facing mounting cost pressure. Factory operating costs have risen due to gas and electricity shortages, higher fuel prices, elevated borrowing costs, more expensive raw materials and other production-related expenses. Energy shortages have been particularly disruptive. In April this year, the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said production capacity at many factories had fallen by 25 to 30 percent because of inadequate gas and electricity supply. title_ko: Toray, 재활용 함량이 거의 93%인 폴리에스터-나일론 섬유 개발
summary: New ARTIROSA® CX textile combines high recycled-material content with premium aesthetics and functional performance, targeting outerwear and urban outdoor applications from Autumn/Winter 2027. Toray Industries, Inc. has developed a polyester-nylon… The post Toray develops polyester-nylon fibre with almost 93% recycled content appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: New ARTIROSA® CX textile combines high recycled-material content with premium aesthetics and functional performance, targeting outerwear and urban outdoor applications from Autumn/Winter 2027. Toray Industries, Inc. has developed a polyester-nylon composite fibre containing at least 93% recycled material by mass, marking a significant step towards incorporating higher levels of recycled raw materials into sophisticated textile products. The development builds on the company’s expertise in polymer design and composite spinning, drawing on technologies cultivated through its recycled fibre brand. The 93% recycled-content figure applies to the newly developed raw yarn, calculated against its total weight. It does not represent the recycled content of the finished fabric or garment, which will vary according to the material composition. Overcoming Challenges in Composite Fibre Development Composite fibres are valued for their ability to deliver enhanced functionality, sophisticated textures and distinctive visual effects. However, incorporating different polymers into a single fibre presents challenges when manufacturers seek to maximise recycled-material content while maintaining consistent quality. Toray has addressed this challenge through its proprietary polymer design and composite spinning technologies, incorporating recycled raw materials into both the polyester and nylon components of the newly developed fibre. The company plans to verify the technology’s viability for mass production while continuing research to increase the recycled-material content of composite fibres. title: Andritz to supply PTFE filter line to China
title_ko: 안드리츠, 중국에 PTFE 필터 라인 공급
summary: Shandong Huazhe has placed an order with Andritz for a high-speed needlepunch line to produce advanced filtration materials. The line will be installed at the company’s headquarters in Jinan, Shandong Province, China. This order builds on the cooperation between the two companies that began in 2023 with the contract for an Andritz batt forming line, […] The post Andritz to supply PTFE filter line to China appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Shandong Huazhe has placed an order with Andritz for a high-speed needlepunch line to produce advanced filtration materials. The line will be installed at the company’s headquarters in Jinan, Shandong Province, China. This order builds on the cooperation between the two companies that began in 2023 with the contract for an Andritz batt forming line, which was successfully delivered in 2024. The new line will expand Shandong Huazhe’s production capacity for high-performance filtration materials made from polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) fibres, addressing the growing demand in this market. It is designed for high-speed, stable operation and the gentle handling of fibres, ensuring consistently high product quality. The line will feature the first commercial application of the A-Type needleloom, a new addition to the Andritz needleloom portfolio, combining cost-efficient operation, production flexibility and high product quality. Its random needle pattern capability helps improve material uniformity and performance. It will also be the first PTFE filtration material production line supplied by Andritz. “The production of advanced filtration materials requires reliable equipment and gentle fibre processing,” says Shandong Huazhe CEO Han Fuhe. “Based on our positive experience with Andritz, we are confident that the new needlepunch line will provide the quality, efficiency and process stability we need for our future growth.” Founded in 2015, Shandong Huazhe is a leading provider of filtration solutions, specialising in materials and equipment for solid-liquid separation and industrial dust collection. www.andritz.com The post Andritz to supply PTFE filter line to China appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

title: Spain has overtaken Germany as Bangladesh’s largest EU market for apparel
summary: In July to September of FY2026-27, Bangladesh shipped $1,148.46 million of RMG to Spain and $1,122.98 million to Germany. A year earlier the order was reversed, with Germany at $1,124.70 million and Spain at $1,009.84 million. Total RMG exports to the EU rose 3.33% in the first quarter, from $4,746.10 million to $4,904.02 million, an […] The post Spain has overtaken Germany as Bangladesh’s largest EU market for apparel appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: In July to September of FY2026-27, Bangladesh shipped $1,148.46 million of RMG to Spain and $1,122.98 million to Germany. A year earlier the order was reversed, with Germany at $1,124.70 million and Spain at $1,009.84 million. Total RMG exports to the EU rose 3.33% in the first quarter, from $4,746.10 million to $4,904.02 million, an increase of $157.92 million. Spain accounted for $138.62 million of that, about 88% of the net gain. September alone showed stronger growth, up 5.53% to $1,410.11 million. The five markets split into two groups: Growing: Spain (+13.73%), the Netherlands (+9.02%) and Poland (+5.77%). Poland’s September jump of 30.25% is the sharpest monthly gain on the table. Flat or falling: Germany (-0.15%) and France (-4.91%). The remaining EU countries together fell 2.24%. Author: Mohiuddin Rubel, Founder & CEO, Bangladesh Apparel Voice (BAV) The post Spain has overtaken Germany as Bangladesh’s largest EU market for apparel appeared first on Textile Focus .

content: The Textile Innovation Awards 2026 , a prestigious recognition platform celebrating innovation and excellence in Bangladesh’s textile and apparel industry, was officially launched today through a press conference held today at the Dongyi Sourcing Limited (DSL) Multipurpose Hall in Dhaka. The second edition of the Textile Innovation Awards is designed to recognize organizations and individuals whose innovations create measurable impact in factory operations, technology, product development, sustainability, market development and organizational transformation. The Textile Innovation Awards 2026 will be presented on 13 November 2026. Figure: The Textile Innovation Award 2026 will be evaluated by a distinguished Jury Board comprising industry leaders, academics and professionals. The Award has established itself as an important industry recognition platform following its inaugural edition in 2024, when several prominent textile and apparel manufacturers and organizations were recognized for their achievements in different areas of innovation. Award recipients included Urmi Group for Product Development, Shasha Denims for Marketing or Market Development, Masco Group for Garment Processing, and Coats Bangladesh for HR and Organizational Development. Figure 2: Prof. Dr. Engr. Ayub Nabi Khan, Vice Chancellor, BUFT Building on the success of the first edition, the 2026 Award aims to bring greater visibility to practical innovations being developed and implemented across Bangladesh’s textile and apparel value chain. This year, awards will be considered across eight categories: Process Innovation, Manufacturing Innovation, Technology, Product Development, Marketing or Market Development, Environmental Sustainability, Social Sustainability, and HR and Organizational Development. title: Govt. targets 1.9mn bales of cotton by 2050
summary: Bangladesh plans to increase domestic cotton production from 2.24 lakh to 19 lakh bales by 2050. For this, cotton cultivation will expand from 39 to 53 districts to reduce import dependence and suppor...
content: Bangladesh plans to increase domestic cotton production from 2.24 lakh to 19 lakh bales by 2050. For this, cotton cultivation will expand from 39 to 53 districts to reduce import dependence and support the textile industry. The Cotton Development Board (CDB) has adopted short-, medium- and long-term plans to increase cotton production by 8.5 times, said Md Rezaul Amin, Executive Director, CDB. Under the plan, the board aims to produce 5 lakh bales of lint cotton within four years, increase output to 10 lakh bales by 2040 and reach 19 lakh bales by 2050. The cultivation area is expected to expand to 2 lakh hectares. The new districts proposed for cotton cultivation include Moulvibazar, Habiganj, Cumilla, Chandpur, Noakhali, Lakshmipur, Barishal, Bhola, Barguna, Chattogram, Feni, Cox's Bazar and Nilphamari. Bangladesh remains heavily dependent on imported cotton, reflecting its position as one of the world's leading readymade garments (RMG) exporters. Domestic production currently meets only around 3–4% of the country's annual cotton requirement , estimated at nearly 80 lakh bales. However, officials said local production supplies around 18–20% of cotton consumed for fabrics intended for the domestic market. The CDB plans to expand cultivation in high charlands and shoals, the northwestern Barind region, suitable hilly areas and comparatively less fertile land, including saline- and drought-prone areas. Cotton may also be cultivated in orchards alongside vegetables, pulses and spices. At a meeting with agriculture ministry officials on September 13, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman asked the CDB to prepare a detailed plan after assessing the country's cotton production potential. title: Is There Such A Thing As An Authentic Synthetic Image?
summary: Individual brands have their own idiosyncratic relationships with generated images, but fashion, on aggregate, has embraced the value of synthetic photography for eCommerce in particular - even in the face of cultural polarisation. What’s next? The post Is There Such A Thing As An Authentic Synthetic Image? appeared first on The Interline .
content: THE INTERLINE PODCAST · 55 MIN Is There Such A Thing As An Authentic Synthetic Image? Listen to Is There Such A Thing As An Authentic Synthetic Image? Follow the show Apple Podcasts Spotify Hey. Welcome back to The Interline Podcast. You’re seeing a lot of generated images these days, and I don’t have to know anything about you or where you shop to make that proclamation, because everyone is seeing a lot of generated images right now. That’s because generative AI has very quickly become a massive part of fashion’s imaging pipelines. From the world’s biggest retailers working to automate photography that previously came saddled with super-high overheads, to small brands who suddenly find themselves able to produce PDP content at a scale they couldn’t have before, or to generate campaigns they never would have had the budget to shoot for real, everyone’s reckoning with what it means to be able to create pretty real-ish-looking fashion photography without cameras, models, lighting, locations and so on. In a lot of cases, that reckoning has turned into AI-generated images being just everywhere, labelled and unlabelled. If you park the ethical concerns for a few minutes — and I promise it will just be a few minutes, because we’re coming back to them in this episode — this all makes pretty unavoidable commercial sense. Unlike 3D/CG, which have a high skill floor and require a relatively heavy time investment, anyone with the right tools can generate an on-model image of a garment that’s potentially fit for purpose, depending on what that purpose is, in minutes. I’ve had a few conversations recently with people who’ve called this all essentially a solved problem, or something close to it. content: Bangladesh’s exports to the UK could reach USD 10 billion if its share of the UK import market increases from 0.49% to 1%. Participants emphasized the need to diversify exports beyond RMG, meet international standards, modernize certification processes, ensure regulatory compliance, and address tariff and non-tariff barriers. Against this backdrop, the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) jointly organized a workshop titled “Exporting to the UK: Opportunities Beyond RMG” in collaboration with the Dhaka Chamber of Commerce & Industry (DCCI) and the British High Commission in Bangladesh today at the DCCI Auditorium in Dhaka. The workshop aimed to raise awareness of UK market opportunities, particularly in non-RMG sectors, and promote export diversification and higher-value exports. DCCI President Taskeen Ahmed emphasized the need to diversify Bangladesh’s UK exports beyond RMG by improving product quality, standards compliance, certification, traceability, branding and market intelligence. He also highlighted the importance of utilizing DCTS benefits and addressing tariff and non-tariff barriers to strengthen bilateral trade and investment. James Goldman, Acting High Commissioner of the British High Commission in Bangladesh, highlighted the longstanding UK–Bangladesh partnership, noting that continued UK market access after LDC graduation would provide businesses with the certainty to plan, grow and invest. He encouraged more Bangladeshi businesses to capitalize on these opportunities. title: YarnProof links polyester origin checks to regional trade compliance
title_ko: YarnProof는 폴리에스터 원산지 확인을 지역 무역 규정 준수와 연결합니다.
summary: Eleven polyester filament yarn manufacturers across North and Central America have launched YarnProof, a traceability initiative that uses embedded physical markers to verify yarn origin. The system a...
content: Eleven polyester filament yarn manufacturers across North and Central America have launched YarnProof, a traceability initiative that uses embedded physical markers to verify yarn origin. The system aims to strengthen compliance with regional trade agreements and help brands substantiate sourcing claims. Figure: YarnProof is designed to support the yarn-forward requirements of the Dominican Republic-Central America-United States Free Trade Agreement (CAFTA-DR) and the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). Led by Unifi and powered by FibreTrace technology, YarnProof embeds an invisible, permanent tracer into polyester filament yarn during extrusion. A handheld scanner can detect the marker in yarn, fabric, and finished goods, providing physical evidence of material origin as products move through the supply chain. The initiative includes Aquafil O'Mara, CS America, CS Central America, Nan Ya Plastics America, Premiere Fibers, Sans Americas, Skytex México, Tecnología Textil Avanzada, Textufil, Unifi Manufacturing and United Textiles of America. Trade compliance is a key driver. YarnProof is designed to support the yarn-forward requirements of the Dominican Republic-Central America-United States Free Trade Agreement (CAFTA-DR) and the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). These rules make the origin of yarn and other textile inputs important for determining whether qualifying goods receive preferential trade treatment. The initiative also highlights a wider industry shift toward physical verification. Unifi already uses its FiberPrint tracer in REPREVE recycled fibers, with its U-TRUST system verifying recycled-content claims across the supply chain. title: Light-activated wound patch for targeted drug delivery
title_ko: 표적 약물 전달을 위한 빛 활성화 상처 패치
summary: Researchers at Swiss materials research institute Empa have developed a light-responsive material that could enable wound dressings to deliver precisely controlled doses of antiseptics and other therapeutic agents, potentially improving the treatment of chronic wounds. Developed at Empa’s Biomimetic Membranes and Textiles laboratory in St. Gallen, the technology uses nanoparticles coated with a light-sensitive polymer […] The post Light-activated wound patch for targeted drug delivery appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Researchers at Swiss materials research institute Empa have developed a light-responsive material that could enable wound dressings to deliver precisely controlled doses of antiseptics and other therapeutic agents, potentially improving the treatment of chronic wounds. Developed at Empa’s Biomimetic Membranes and Textiles laboratory in St. Gallen, the technology uses nanoparticles coated with a light-sensitive polymer to release active ingredients when exposed to visible LED light. Switching off the light stops the release, allowing the timing and dosage of treatment to be controlled. The research could have particular significance for patients with diabetes, who are vulnerable to chronic wounds caused by poor circulation and nerve damage. Diabetic foot ulcers can remain open for months, requiring frequent dressing changes, specialist care and repeated hospital visits. The Empa team, led by Luciano Boesel and Giorgia Giovannini, has developed a system based on silica nanoparticles loaded with chlorhexidine, a widely used wound antiseptic. The nanoparticles are surrounded by a polymer coating containing molecular photoswitches that change their structure when exposed to specific wavelengths of visible light. This causes the polymer to swell and become more permeable to water, allowing the disinfectant to escape from the silica core. title: Donghua University develops washable fibers with built-in electronic circuits
title_ko: 동화대학교, 전자회로 내장된 세탁 가능한 섬유 개발
summary: Researchers at Donghua University in Shanghai, China, have developed a programmable microfluidic spinning method that integrates electronic circuits directly into soft fibers. Published in Nature Elec...
content: Researchers at Donghua University in Shanghai, China, have developed a programmable microfluidic spinning method that integrates electronic circuits directly into soft fibers. Published in Nature Electronics by a team led by Professor Zhu Meifang and researcher Wang Gang, the technology enables smart garments that sense, process, and respond to data without external electronic attachments. Conventional electronic textiles rely on conductive yarns to connect separate microchips, sensors, and heating elements. These connections often degrade under mechanical stress from stretching, bending, and laundering. Donghua University addresses this weakness by building functional electronic structures inside the fiber during spinning. The research demonstrates electroluminescent fibers for light emission, resistor and capacitor fibers for signal processing, organic electrochemical transistor fibers for digital logic operations, and functional fibers for touchless sensing. The development aligns with broader advances across material and machinery sectors. Belgian supplier Bekaert manufactures Bekinox stainless steel fibers blended with cotton or polyester for data and energy transmission. German machinery builder ZSK Stickmaschinen uses its EP-30 device to position and connect circuit boards onto textile substrates during embroidery. However, while ZSK attaches components during processing, Donghua University embeds electronic functions within the core fiber structure. Potential applications span healthcare monitoring, athletic performance tracking, industrial protective wear, and soft robotics. Nevertheless, commercial adoption depends on scalable manufacturing. summary: Fashion’s next premium story may be written on the fibre label. As people become more selective about what they buy and wear, the material behind a garment is taking on… The post Growing consumer preference for natural fibres as Woolmark launches Return to Real appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: Fashion’s next premium story may be written on the fibre label. As people become more selective about what they buy and wear, the material behind a garment is taking on new importance. New research commissioned to Ipsos by Woolmark across the United States, France, Germany, Italy and China found that on average, 82% of consumers would choose natural fibres over synthetic alternatives when price, style and fit are equal. Merinowool was preferred to polyester in every market surveyed, with an average preference of 65%. The findings point to a wider shift in fashion. Worldwide Google search interest in “Merinowool” has more than doubled over the past five years, with momentum continuing to build over the past 12 months. Fibre is no longer simply a technical or sourcing decision. It is becoming part of how consumers understand quality, performance and value. “Consumers want to know what a garment is made from, what that means in everyday use and whether the claims can be trusted,” said Woolmark Managing Director Bryan Fry. “That puts fibre, and the evidence behind it, back at the centre of the conversation.” Merino wool’s strongest distinction is its association with premium quality. In the latest Ipsos research, it ranked first for both premium and high quality in four of the five markets surveyed. The survey also reveals that citizens are prepared to pay for the difference. On average across the five markets, 67% say they would pay more for clothing made mainly from natural fibres. Merino wool’s premium perception is increasingly supported by its performance credentials. Brands are taking the fibre beyond traditional tailoring and knitwear into technical sportswear and elevated essentials for a more refined material story. The program includes seminars featuring presentations by Italian companies, B2B meetings with local industry representatives and visits to local production facilities. Organised by the Italian Trade Agency in collaboration with ACIMIT, the Association of Italian Textile Machinery Manufacturers, and Confindustria Moda, the […] The post Italian textile machinery manufacturers target Brazil appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: A delegation of 22 Italian companies will visit Brazil from 19 to 24 October 2026 as part of a trade mission aimed at strengthening commercial and industrial cooperation between the two countries’ textile sectors. Organised by the Italian Trade Agency in collaboration with ACIMIT, the Association of Italian Textile Machinery Manufacturers, and Confindustria Moda, the initiative will include workshops on 20 October in Santa Catarina and 22 October in São Paulo. The delegation comprises 18 textile machinery manufacturers alongside companies specialising in yarns, fabrics and clothing accessories, representing expertise across the Italian textile supply chain. The programme will feature technical presentations, business-to-business meetings with Brazilian manufacturers and visits to local production facilities. Activities in Santa Catarina will cover the textile manufacturing centres of Blumenau, Joinville and Brusque, while the São Paulo programme will include Americana and Denim City São Paulo, an important hub for textile and denim innovation. Brazil remains a strategically important market for Italian textile machinery manufacturers. Exports to the country reached €48 million in 2025, with a further €20 million recorded during the first half of 2026. Brazil currently ranks tenth among the industry’s leading export destinations. Finishing machinery accounts for the largest share of Italian textile machinery exports to Brazil at 57%, followed by accessories and other machinery, each representing 11%. Knitting machinery accounts for 10%, highlighting opportunities for Italian technology suppliers serving Brazil’s established knitwear and textile manufacturing industries. title: Texverse 2.0 to be held on October 30 at BUTEX
summary: The Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX) will host the national competition ‘Texverse 2.0’ on October 30, bringing together students from universities, textile engineering colleges and higher sec...
content: The Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX) will host the national competition ‘Texverse 2.0’ on October 30, bringing together students from universities, textile engineering colleges and higher secondary institutions for competitions centered on research, innovation, creativity and problem-solving. Organized by the BUTEX Science Club, the day-long event will begin at 8:00am and continue until evening. Different segments of the competition will be held at the university’s Auditorium, Seminar Room, Academic Building and Central Field, while some competitions will be conducted online. The event has so far established collaboration with 25 student clubs and organizations from different universities and textile colleges across the country. These include KUET Textile Club, BUP Career Club, Textile Club-MBSTU, DUET Textile Career & Research Club, NITER Science Society, BUFT Career Development Club, Daffodil AI Club, Southeast University Textile Club (SEUTC), Green University Textile Club (GUTC), Sonargaon University Textile Club and RTEC Research Club, among others. The competition aims to encourage students to engage in research and innovation while developing practical and sustainable solutions to challenges faced by the textile sector. It will also provide participants with a platform to showcase their creative ideas, technical knowledge and problem-solving abilities. At the university level, the competition will feature a project exhibition, research-based poster presentation, quiz competition, textile case competition, treasure hunt, essay writing and an artificial intelligence-based video-making competition. title: Fresh Pressure, Same Promise – Analysing The CLO EU Summit 2026
summary: Reflections on Europe's milestone 3D / DPC summit, at a time when the shape, scope, and outlook for digital design, development, and production is changing incredibly quickly. The post Fresh Pressure, Same Promise – Analysing The CLO EU Summit 2026 appeared first on The Interline .
content: I’ve been an advocate of 3D for most of my career. But as I made my way to Munich in mid-September to host CLO’s EU Summit for the second year running, I couldn’t shake the sense that digital product creation was on a downswing. I knew I’d be seeing a bunch of familiar faces. But some of the people who had been on stage with me a year earlier, representing 3D teams at major brands, would not be coming back. Not because they were too busy transforming end-to-end operations, but because their companies had since scaled back their departments. In some cases they’d eliminated them. I knew I’d see new capabilities, new advances in usability, and fresh features for a demanding userbase who’ve been using CLO as a canvas for design, development, and simulation for decades. But I still found myself in a mindset that I know a lot of brands, suppliers, and DPC ecosystem vendors share: I wondered whether a different class of technology was casting such a long, deep shadow that maybe those latest steps forward wouldn’t really end up mattering all that much. CLO User Summit Munich 2026, CLO Virtual Fashion. That’s a big change in sentiment and situation in just twelve months. I left last year’s CLO summit optimistic about the outlook for DPC, and separately very interested in AI – but I didn’t expect the two to end up smashing into each other quite as promptly or as comprehensively as they since have. title: Asad Sattar Puts Bangladeshi Fashion and Arka in the Global Conversation at BRICS+Fashion Summit, Moscow
summary: For the second consecutive year, Asad Sattar, founder and creative director of Arka Fashion Week, represented Bangladesh at BRICS+ Fashion Summit in Moscow, Russia, held from September 28 to 30, 2026. He spoke at the Summit’s plenary session on the role of fashion in shaping culture, and on fashion as a tool for soft power. […] The post Asad Sattar Puts Bangladeshi Fashion and Arka in the Global Conversation at BRICS+Fashion Summit, Moscow appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: For the second consecutive year, Asad Sattar, founder and creative director of Arka Fashion Week, represented Bangladesh at BRICS+ Fashion Summit in Moscow, Russia, held from September 28 to 30, 2026. He spoke at the Summit’s plenary session on the role of fashion in shaping culture, and on fashion as a tool for soft power. In his session, Asad discussed how Bangladesh, known internationally for its garment manufacturing, can use fashion to carry its culture, crafts and stories to audiences abroad. He talks not only about the pull soft power has, but also explains how fashion can often be an entry point into art for many people. “Fashion is a getaway art. It’s the front door – for most people, their first art form, because not everyone can paint or play an instrument, but everyone gets dressed in the morning.” Arka Fashion plays a key role in the growth of an ecosystem amenable to creativity and innovation in fashion. This is a boon for Bangladesh, which has a history of being providers of ready made garments, but not leaders in design. Sattar explains, “For forty years Bangladesh has been ‘Made in Bangladesh’ – we make what the world designs.‘Designed in Bangladesh’ is a different proposition entirely: a garment carries a price, but a design carries a point of view. And a point of view travels further than any trade delegation.” This philosophy is embedded in the very name of “Arka”, which translates to the sun. Connecting this to the notion of soft power, Sattar mentions his belief that it is necessary to emulate the sun and not a spotlight, with the latter shining a light on one person, and the former rising every day. summary: Bcomp has partnered with Polestar to bring its lightweight bio-based materials into the new Polestar 5 four-door electric grand tourer (GT). The collaboration between the two companies began during the development of the Polestar […] The post Polestar adds a signature weave appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Bcomp has partnered with Polestar to bring its lightweight bio-based materials into the new Polestar 5 four-door electric grand tourer (GT). The vehicle features Bcomp’s ampliTex and powerRibs technologies in the front seatbacks and tailgate structure, reducing the use of virgin plastics. The collaboration between the two companies began during the development of the Polestar Precept, a concept car, and evolved into large-scale production for the Polestar 5. Together, the companies developed a bespoke ampliTex flax fabric known as the ‘Polestar Signature Weave’, designed to serve both structural and aesthetic functions in the interior cabin. This material has since become a defining feature of Polestar’s minimalist and transparent design approach, engineered and tested for durability and performance across thousands of cars in global markets. Polestar credits Bcomp’s flax-based composites with using 50% less fossil-based material and being up to 40% lighter than the traditional plastics they replace. Depending on the application, Bcomp’s natural fibre composites can also reduce the cradle-to-gate CO2 footprint of components by up to 60%. All Bcomp components used in the vehicle have been validated to meet stringent automotive standards for durability, safety, UV resistance, scratch resistance and long-term ageing performance. © Bcomp “Working with Polestar over a number of years has given us the opportunity to show that the path from a material concept to a series-production component can be long and rigorous but is ultimately worth it,” says Per Martensson, chief revenue officer at Bcomp. “The Polestar 5 seatbacks have a combination of lightweighting performance, reduced carbon footprint and design for end-of-life that conventional composites cannot offer. summary: This year’s program adds an honorarium for three students who performed well in SSC TEAM Group has awarded the Wahid-Kohinoor Memorial Scholarship 2026 to 36 meritorious students of Hazi Piar Ali School, the school located adjacent to its 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd. facility in Savar. The annual ceremony was graced by the presence of Managing […] The post TEAM Group Awards Wahid-Kohinoor Memorial Scholarship to 36 Students of Hazi Piar Ali School appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: This year’s program adds an honorarium for three students who performed well in SSC TEAM Group has awarded the Wahid-Kohinoor Memorial Scholarship 2026 to 36 meritorious students of Hazi Piar Ali School, the school located adjacent to its 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd. facility in Savar. The annual ceremony was graced by the presence of Managing Director Afroza Shaheen and Deputy Managing Director Abdullah Hil Nakib. This year, 18 primary-level students (KG to Class 5), 15 high-school students (Classes 6 to 10) and 3 SSC graduates were recognized. At both the primary and high-school levels, the scholarship was awarded on merit by position, with the first, second, and third position-holders of each class from KG to Class 10 receiving the award. New this year: Three students who achieved good results in the SSC examination also received an honorarium, extending the program’s recognition beyond the school’s regular classes. A high-level delegation from the Kingdom of the Netherlands – Mr. Steven Collet, Vice Minister for International Cooperation; Ms. Wampie Libon, Ambassador for Sustainable Development; and Ambassador Joris van Bommel – visited 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd., TEAM Group’s LEED Platinum-certified facility, to see how investments and Dutch-Bangladesh partnerships are advancing sustainability in the textile sector. The delegation briefly joined the scholarship event as the program began, before departing. Addressing the students, Managing Director Afroza Shaheen urged them to carry their values as far as their grades. “You have already proven yourselves through your merit and achievements. title: Performance Days expands to third hall amid record demand
summary: MUNICH – Performance Days has expanded into a third exhibition hall for the first time, with almost 600 exhibitors at its October 2026 edition. The show also sees the launch of a new Sustainability Exchange focused on regulation, circularity and industry collaboration. The functional fabrics trade fair, taking place on 13–14 October at Messe München, [...] The post Performance Days expands to third hall amid record demand appeared first on Apparel Insider .
content: MUNICH – Performance Days has expanded into a third exhibition hall for the first time, with almost 600 exhibitors at its October 2026 edition. The show also sees the launch of a new Sustainability Exchange focused on regulation, circularity and industry collaboration. The functional fabrics trade fair, taking place on 13–14 October at Messe München, covers approximately 27,500 square metres, making it the largest edition in the event’s history. Organisers said the expansion follows record exhibitor demand, with space nearly sold out several months ahead of the event. Major companies exhibiting for the first time include W. L. Gore & Associates, Youngone Corporation, Hyundai Chemical and Linz Textil. “Performance Days is currently experiencing the strongest demand in its history,” said CEO Marco Weichert. “Expanding into three halls reflects the importance the platform has gained within the international industry.” The additional space will accommodate new exhibitors, specialist areas and technical forums covering material innovation and garment technologies. The event will also introduce the Sustainability Exchange, a dedicated area bringing together organisations working on certification, traceability, textile recycling, responsible sourcing and regulatory compliance. Confirmed participants include bluesign, Control Union, Fashion for Good, Global Standard, Hohenstein, RETRAKT and China Textile Recycling. The initiative is intended to help businesses respond to increasingly complex sustainability requirements, including the EU’s Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR), Digital Product Passports and EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR). “Sustainability is no longer a specialist topic. title: Global hosiery market projected to reach $57.4 bn by 2034
summary: The global hosiery market is steadily shifting from basic volume production toward functional specialization. According to a market report by Research Nester, the sector was valued at $44.16 billion i...
content: The global hosiery market is steadily shifting from basic volume production toward functional specialization. According to a market report by Research Nester, the sector was valued at $44.16 billion in 2025 and is set to rise from $45.46 billion in 2026 to $57.37 billion by 2034. This steady trajectory reflects a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 2.95% over the forecast period. Figure: Regionally, Europe led the global landscape with a commanding 30% market share, underscoring strong consumer preference for high-value technical legwear. Detailed market data from Fortune Business Insights shows that traditional socks remain the dominant product type, capturing approximately 35% of the total hosiery market share. Meanwhile, men's hosiery holds around 30% of the market share, driven by rising demand for professional dress socks and performance-oriented cushioning. Regionally, Europe led the global landscape with a commanding 30% market share, underscoring strong consumer preference for high-value technical legwear. This evolution is heavily propelled by consumer demand for products that merge comfort, functionality, and sustainability. Modern buyers increasingly seek out moisture-wicking fibers, seamless construction, and body-shaping technology for daily wear and athleisure. These high-performance segments provide manufacturers with clear opportunities for product differentiation and healthier profit margins. For Bangladesh's textile and apparel industry, these numbers signal a critical pathway to diversify beyond basic knitwear exports. Local manufacturers can leverage advanced yarn selection and specialized knitting technologies to tap into the expanding global demand for technical hosiery.

summary: British textile innovator MAXXAM Textiles and East London-based garment manufacturer ApparelTASKER will return to Cannes later this month for Mare di Moda 2026, the international exhibition for swimwear, lingerie and athleisure fabrics, with an expanded collection of stretch textiles and garments for Summer 2027. The event, taking place from 27-29 October, will provide a European […] The post MAXXAM and ApparelTASKER return to Cannes appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: British textile innovator MAXXAM Textiles and East London-based garment manufacturer ApparelTASKER will return to Cannes later this month for Mare di Moda 2026, the international exhibition for swimwear, lingerie and athleisure fabrics, with an expanded collection of stretch textiles and garments for Summer 2027. The event, taking place from 27-29 October, will provide a European showcase for the British partnership, which was formed at Mare di Moda just one year ago and has since developed new garment applications for MAXXAM’s distinctive crinkle-textured stretch fabric. Created by textile designer Rosemary Moore in the early 1980s, MAXXAM is a seamless, four-way stretch textile with a three-dimensional crinkled surface that expands and contracts to accommodate different body shapes. The innovation is represented in the permanent collection of London’s Victoria and Albert Museum. MAXXAM founder and textile designer Rosemary Moore. © MAXXAM Textiles For Summer 2027, the companies will present new garment silhouettes and a vibrant colour palette featuring citrus orange, lime green and bright red, demonstrating the textile’s versatility in contemporary fashion applications. The collaboration began when Moore met ApparelTASKER founder Zack Sartor at Mare di Moda in 2025. Their shared interest in textile innovation, responsible manufacturing and garment development has since evolved into an ongoing partnership. “What started with a conversation between Zack and me has developed into something really creative, and we’re continuing to discover new possibilities for MAXXAM textiles through colour, shape and garment design,” said Moore. “I’ve always believed that heritage and innovation should sit side by side. title: Chinese firm to invest $17m in Mongla EPZ garment factory
summary: Chinese company Longteng Garment Co Ltd will invest US$17 million to set up a garment factory at Mongla Export Processing Zone (EPZ), creating employment for more than 3,000 Bangladeshis. The Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) signed a land lease agreement with the company on Monday at its complex in Dhaka to facilitate the investment, […] The post Chinese firm to invest $17m in Mongla EPZ garment factory appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Chinese company Longteng Garment Co Ltd will invest US$17 million to set up a garment factory at Mongla Export Processing Zone (EPZ), creating employment for more than 3,000 Bangladeshis. The Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) signed a land lease agreement with the company on Monday at its complex in Dhaka to facilitate the investment, according to a press release. Md Tanvir Hossain, member (Investment Promotion) of BEPZA, and Lin Qiangqiang, chairman of Longteng Garment, signed the agreement on behalf of their respective organisations. BEPZA Executive Chairman Maj Gen Mohammad Moazzem Hossain and senior officials witnessed the signing ceremony. The company will establish its factory on 16,426.37 square metres of land, with an annual production capacity of six million pieces of innerwear. Its products will be supplied to international brands and retailers, including Aerie, Calvin Klein, Zara, Florence & Fred, ASOS and Primark. The company also listed major buyers such as H&M, Walmart, Marks & Spencer and Gap. Longteng Garment plans to export its products to markets across the world, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Europe, Australia, Canada, Japan, Brazil, Mexico, Chile, Algeria and Iraq. Welcoming the investment, BEPZA Executive Chairman Maj Gen Mohammad Moazzem Hossain thanked the company for choosing Bangladesh and expressing confidence in the country’s investment potential. He assured the investor of BEPZA’s necessary support and cooperation to facilitate the establishment and smooth operation of the factory. title: Polish Defence and Uniform Manufacturer UNIFEQ Europe Adopts Coats Digital’s GSDCost and AI-Powered GSDQuest to Support Rapid Growth
summary: Investment in next-generation costing technology will improve sewing-floor productivity, accelerate tender costing and create a trusted standard for performance and fair operator rewards. content: WARSAW, POLAND and LONDON, UK – 14, OCTOBER 2026 – Coats Digital is pleased to announce that rapidly growing Polish defence and uniform manufacturer UNIFEQ Europe Sp. z o.o. has invested in its award-winning GSDCost solution together with its AI-powered GSDQuest platform to establish a consistent approach to garment costing, improve sewing-floor productivity and accelerate labour costing for tenders and new products. The implementation is focused initially on UNIFEQ Europe’s apparel and uniform manufacturing plant in Kętrzyn, where GSDCost will establish standard minute values (SMVs) for core uniform styles, support line balancing and capacity planning, and provide the foundation for a new performance-related bonus scheme for production operators. GSDQuest will enable the company to generate fast, AI-powered first-pass Bills of Labour from garment images. Founded in 2011, UNIFEQ Europe is an independent Polish family-owned manufacturer specialising in military and uniformed-services apparel, tactical equipment and individual ballistic protection. The company supplies armed forces and uniformed services across Poland and Europe, with recent major contract wins including the Swedish Police and the armed forces of Sweden and France. With annual turnover exceeding PLN 240 million (approximately USD 60–65 million), UNIFEQ Europe is experiencing rapid growth and was recognised among Poland’s fastest-growing companies in the Forbes Diamonds 2025 ranking. The company is also investing millions of PLN in expanding its Kętrzyn operation, including a new ballistic protection production line, R&D department and in-house ballistic laboratory. content: Welspun Living is taking another step towards intelligent manufacturing with the launch of WelVisionAi, an AI-powered computer vision initiative designed to bring artificial intelligence directly to the shop floor. Developed through the Welspun USA Operations and IT teams, WelVisionAi transforms live manufacturing activity into continuous, actionable intelligence. By using computer vision to observe and analyse shop-floor operations, the system can see, measure and identify patterns across manufacturing processes. The initiative is designed to provide greater visibility into key operational parameters, including production output, machine utilisation, throughput, efficiency and safety. By converting real-time factory activity into meaningful intelligence, WelVisionAi can help manufacturing teams identify patterns, respond faster and continuously improve operations. The initiative reflects Welspun Living’s broader ambition to build a more visible, connected, intelligent and responsive manufacturing environment, where people, data and technology work together to strengthen operational capabilities. Brand-Promotion According to Mr. Keyur Parekh, the initiative represents the next phase of Welspun’s manufacturing journey, bringing AI “from the screen to the shop floor.” The broader vision of Welspun Living, under Dipali Goenka, Managing Director & CEO, is to continually evolve the organisation by harnessing technology, innovation and human ingenuity to build stronger capabilities and unlock new possibilities. WelVisionAi marks the beginning of this journey, with AI moving beyond a technology concept to become an integral layer of intelligence within manufacturing operations. Moynul Hassan Shibly , whose leadership supported the initiative to connect students’ theoretical knowledge with practical industrial experience. The visit aimed to bridge the gap between classroom learning and real-world industrial practices. Through this initiative, students explored the industrial working environment, developed a better understanding of manufacturing operations, and gained insights into the practical applications of their academic knowledge. Industrial visits play an important role in textile education by allowing students to observe industry practices beyond textbooks and laboratory sessions. Such experiences help them understand production processes, workplace requirements, and the professional skills needed to build successful careers in the textile and apparel sector. The joint initiative by Textile Club and Lalmonirhat Textile Institute reflects their commitment to enhancing students’ practical knowledge and strengthening connections between academic institutions and the industry. The visit to Arunima Sportswear Limited offered participating students a valuable learning opportunity, encouraging them to connect theoretical concepts with industrial experience and prepare for future professional challenges in the textile and apparel industry. title: Cyclothe targets missing links in recycling
title_ko: Cyclothe는 재활용 과정에서 누락된 고리를 겨냥합니다.
summary: Swedish technology company Cyclothe is developing an integrated system for collecting, identifying and sorting discarded textiles, with the aim of addressing one of the biggest obstacles to Europe’s emerging circular textile economy – the lack of infrastructure connecting waste collection with commercially viable reuse and recycling operations. The company’s approach combines smart collection points, automated […] The post Cyclothe targets missing links in recycling appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Swedish technology company Cyclothe is developing an integrated system for collecting, identifying and sorting discarded textiles, with the aim of addressing one of the biggest obstacles to Europe’s emerging circular textile economy – the lack of infrastructure connecting waste collection with commercially viable reuse and recycling operations. The company’s approach combines smart collection points, automated material identification, AI-supported sorting decisions and digital traceability to direct discarded textiles towards their most appropriate destinations. Rather than concentrating exclusively on recycling, Cyclothe aims to prioritise reuse, repair and resale wherever possible, before directing materials that cannot be recovered in these ways towards textile recycling operations. The intention is to connect consumers, retailers, municipalities, logistics providers and recycling companies through a common physical and digital infrastructure, enabling collected materials to be identified, tracked and channelled into appropriate markets. The mandatory separate collection of textiles was introduced in Europe at the beginning of 2025, but the infrastructure needed to process the resulting material streams remains fragmented. The introduction of extended producer responsibility (EPR) requirements is expected to increase pressure on brands and retailers to participate in more effective systems for recovering discarded products. Cyclothe is now preparing to expand its technology across the Nordic countries and wider Europe, appointing Calvin Woolley, formerly sustainable business manager for textiles at Inter Ikea, as co-founder and CEO to lead the next stage of its development. summary: Woolmark, the global authority on wool fibre certification and promotion, is putting Merino wool’s natural performance credentials at the centre of a new international campaign, backed by consumer research showing a strong preference for natural fibres over synthetics. The Australian wool industry’s marketing and certification organisation has launched Return to Real following an Ipsos study […] The post Consumers favour natural fibres, says Woolmark appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Woolmark, the global authority on wool fibre certification and promotion, is putting Merino wool’s natural performance credentials at the centre of a new international campaign, backed by consumer research showing a strong preference for natural fibres over synthetics. The Australian wool industry’s marketing and certification organisation has launched Return to Real following an Ipsos study across the United States, France, Germany, Italy and China, which found that 82% of consumers would choose natural fibres over synthetics when price, style and fit are equal. Merino wool was preferred to polyester in all five markets, with an average preference of 65%, while 67% of respondents said they would pay more for clothing made mainly from natural fibres. “Consumers want to know what a garment is made from, what that means in everyday use and whether the claims can be trusted,” said Woolmark Managing Director Bryan Fry. “That puts fibre, and the evidence behind it, back at the centre of the conversation.” Merino wool ranked first for both premium and high quality perceptions in four of the five markets surveyed. Meanwhile, 71% of respondents considered independent certification or verification of fibre content and quality important, while 45% said fibre composition had become more important in their purchasing decisions. Beyond traditional Woolmark says growing interest in natural materials is creating opportunities for Merino wool beyond traditional knitwear and tailoring, particularly in technical sportswear, performance apparel and premium everyday clothing. Global Google search interest in Merino wool has more than doubled over the past five years. title_ko: 새로운 PLA를 사용하여 meltblown 라인에서 95% 이상의 효율성 달성
summary: TotalEnergies Corbion, headquartered in Gorinchem, the Netherlands, has commercially launched a new polylactic acid (PLA) grade specifically developed for meltblown nonwoven filter media, following industrial trials demonstrating filtration efficiencies exceeding 95%. The new Luminy L040 grade can be processed on existing meltblown production lines without major equipment modifications, enabling manufacturers to produce ultra-fine fibres with […] The post Over 95% efficiency on meltblown lines with new PLA appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: TotalEnergies Corbion, headquartered in Gorinchem, the Netherlands, has commercially launched a new polylactic acid (PLA) grade specifically developed for meltblown nonwoven filter media, following industrial trials demonstrating filtration efficiencies exceeding 95%. The new Luminy L040 grade can be processed on existing meltblown production lines without major equipment modifications, enabling manufacturers to produce ultra-fine fibres with diameters of one micron or less from a biobased alternative to conventional polypropylene (PP). A key characteristic of the material is its ability to retain an electrostatic charge, which is essential for capturing fine airborne particles without creating excessive resistance to airflow. The combination of ultra-low viscosity and electrostatic properties enables high-efficiency filter media to be produced without the degrading agents or electrostatic additives that would otherwise be required. “During the early-access programme, industrial partners including Hansae in South Korea successfully processed Luminy L040 on commercial meltblown lines, demonstrating stable production, ultra-fine fibre formation and filtration efficiencies exceeding 95%,” says Bert Clymans, EMEA senior business development and nonwovens market segment leader at TotalEnergies Corbion. The launch also follows independent research by the University of Michigan indicating that PLA-based meltblown media can achieve filtration performance comparable to conventional PP materials. Made from annually renewable feedstocks, the new PLA grade is said to have a carbon footprint more than 80% lower than PP, offering filter manufacturers a potential route to reducing the embodied emissions of their products. title: EURATEX urges Member States to prioritise competitiveness in the next EU budget
summary: Brussels, 14 October 2026 – Ahead of crucial discussions among EU Member States on the next Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) for 2028–2034, EURATEX, the European Apparel and Textile Confederation, calls on European leaders to safeguard ambitious funding for industrial competitiveness and ensure that these resources translate into concrete investment support in European companies. With Europe… Read more The post EURATEX urges Member States to prioritise competitiveness in the next EU budget appeared first on EURATEX .
content: Brussels, 14 October 2026 – Ahead of crucial discussions among EU Member States on the next Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) for 2028–2034, EURATEX, the European Apparel and Textile Confederation, calls on European leaders to safeguard ambitious funding for industrial competitiveness and ensure that these resources translate into concrete investment support in European companies. With Europe facing increasing global competition, high energy costs and a weakening industrial base, EURATEX warns that reducing the resources available for competitiveness would undermine the EU’s ambition to implement the recommendations of the Draghi Report and strengthen European industry. The European textile and clothing industry, representing nearly 200,000 companies, 1.2 million workers and €166 billion in annual turnover, illustrates the urgency of this challenge : companies are expected to invest simultaneously in decarbonisation, circularity, digitalisation and innovation, while facing growing competition from lower-cost imports. The new MFF should help them to make these investments. Dirk Vantyghem, Director General of EURATEX, commented: “Europe has recognised the urgent need to restore its industrial competitiveness. The next EU budget must now turn that ambition into action. We need a strong European Competitiveness Fund that supports companies in investing, innovating and maintaining manufacturing capacity in Europe. But money alone is not enough: competitiveness starts with a regulatory framework that rewards entrepreneurship, reduces unnecessary burdens and guarantees fair competition. title: EU rules push textile firms to prove sustainability claims with product data
summary: EU sustainability regulations are raising the bar for textile and apparel companies, requiring stronger evidence to support environmental claims and improve product traceability. Figure: The European...
content: EU sustainability regulations are raising the bar for textile and apparel companies, requiring stronger evidence to support environmental claims and improve product traceability. Figure: The European Commission reports that 53% of green claims are vague, misleading, or unfounded, while 40% lack supporting evidence. At Performance Days in Munich on October 13, consultants urged companies to connect product-level data across design, production, use, and end-of-life management. The shift puts greater emphasis on verifiable evidence rather than sustainability labels alone. For Bangladesh’s apparel exporters, this means preparing reliable data on fiber composition, recycled content, energy and water use, emissions and chemical management to meet evolving buyer and regulatory requirements. The EU’s Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) provides the framework for Digital Product Passports (DPPs). The European Commission’s indicative timeline schedules the adoption of textile-specific rules for the fourth quarter of 2027, followed by a transition period of at least 18 months. Green claims also face scrutiny. The European Commission reports that 53% of green claims are vague, misleading or unfounded, while 40% lack supporting evidence. Companies must therefore ensure that environmental statements are specific, measurable and backed by reliable records. For textile manufacturers, the priority is to connect supplier records, production data and environmental performance in a traceable system. Early preparation can help Bangladesh’s exporters respond to buyer demands, reduce compliance risks and remain ready for evolving EU market requirements.

content: Starting from the upcoming Spring Edition of Intertextile Shanghai Apparel Fabrics – set to take place from 10 to 12 March 2027 – the organisers have signalled their intention to anchor the show’s evolving positioning with a new slogan: Shape the Movement. Equipped with its refined focus, Intertextile Apparel is set to showcase its continued importance for defining the industry’s future – from creating and implementing new trends, to exchanging cultural ideas, functional utility and eco-innovation, to enabling business deals with far-reaching economic benefits. Several high-potential areas have been earmarked for further development next spring. New slogan ‘Shape the Movement’ and key visual for Intertextile Shanghai Apparel Fabrics – Spring Edition 2027 (second from right) alongside other textile fairs’ wallscapes at NECC this autumn (Source: Messe Frankfurt) The fair’s key themes Fashion Forward, Textile Future, Performance Textiles, and Sustainability will again reflect the demands of the global textile market, with the latter two showing especially strong potential in the current landscape. Ms Wilmet Shea, General Manager of Messe Frankfurt (HK) Ltd , commented: “Shaping the industry’s movement is exactly what this fair does, at every edition. The new slogan is a nod to Intertextile Apparel’s unmatched influence in determining what vast numbers of global consumers want to wear, how they want to wear it, and how industry players can make that happen. Over 400 attendees came from a range of […] The post Spinning a good yarn appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Fiber Extrusion Technology Limited (FET) took a major role at the Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress in Austria in September, with Dr Jonny Hunter presenting “Spinning a good yarn.” The exhibition brought together over 100 expert speakers, leading innovators, and global stakeholders for a focused program of events. Over 400 attendees came from a range of industrial and academic organizations. Industrial examples included Barmag, Sembis, and Fraunhofer, while from the academic world CETI (France), Aachen (Germany), Fibernamics (Portugal), and many others were present. As global challenges mount – from decarbonization pressures to shifting markets – this year’s congress reaffirmed its role as a key platform for forward-looking solutions and collaborative progress. Hunter’s presentation took a broad view of the immense challenges and innovations that have emerged in the fiber industry over recent years. FET has been at the forefront of many of these innovations – designing, developing, and manufacturing bespoke fiber equipment, thus enabling customers in a wide range of industries to find solutions to their individual challenges. FET’s reputation has been founded predominantly on melt spinning solutions – in multifilament, monofilament and nonwoven formats – and the first part of the presentation highlighted this aspect. However, FET’s more recent success has been grounded in further niche developments and technological variations: Meltblown systems for non-continuous nonwoven fibers. Spunbond equipment for continuous nonwovens. Wet spinning systems, where melt spinning solutions are not possible. content: Mayer & Cie. Global will focus on mattress ticking production and fine-gauge double-face fabrics at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026, taking place in Shanghai from 20-24 November. The German circular knitting machine manufacturer will showcase two established models, introduce its new portfolio strategy and provide an update on machinery development at its Albstadt headquarters. Taking centre stage will be the OVJA 2.4 EM, a high-productivity circular knitting machine designed for mattress ticking, alongside the OV 3.2 QCe, configured to produce double-face fabrics in the exceptionally fine E40 gauge. The OVJA 2.4 EM. © Mayer & Cie. Global “Around 70 per cent of the world’s mattress fabric production takes place in China,” said Alton Xu, CEO of Mayer & Cie. Global. “Our OVJA family offers excellent solutions for this application. The OVJA 2.4 EM in particular combines maximum output with extensive patterning options.” The OVJA 2.4 EM produces up to 30kg of fabric per hour, supported by a feeder density of 2.4 feeders per inch. Its horizontal weft yarn guide facilitates operation and rapid changeovers, while improved yarn guidance and a pneumatic cross-flow nozzle maintain consistent yarn tension at high speeds, minimising vibration and ensuring reliable yarn feeding. Electronic individual needle selection in the cylinder provides extensive patterning possibilities and enables rapid design changes, making the machine particularly suitable for the demanding mattress ticking market. The OVJA 2.4 EM offers a wide variety of patterns. © Mayer & Cie. title: ISRA Trade & Services Bangladesh hosts industry networking event with Vice President of KAISHAN Group
summary: ISRA Trade & Services Bangladesh, the sole distributor of KAISHAN in Bangladesh, hosted an evening of discussion, networking and collaboration on 13 October at Hotel Amari, Dhaka, marking the visi...
content: ISRA Trade & Services Bangladesh, the sole distributor of KAISHAN in Bangladesh, hosted an evening of discussion, networking and collaboration on 13 October at Hotel Amari, Dhaka, marking the visit of Cui Feng, Group Vice President of Global KAISHAN Group. The event brought together prominent leaders, industry representatives and business stakeholders from Bangladesh’s textile and apparel sector, alongside representatives of industrial machinery and technology companies. The gathering provided a platform to discuss industrial solutions, operational efficiency and potential business collaborations. Mohammad Shahab Uddin Sikder, CEO of ISRA Trade & Services Bangladesh, hosted the event, which featured a presentation by Cui Feng on KAISHAN Group, its services and business activities, highlighting the company's industrial capabilities and solutions. Figure 01: Cui Feng, Group Vice President of Global KAISHAN Group. Focus on cost efficiency and industrial competitiveness In the opening remarks, Mohammad Shahab Uddin Sikder highlighted the importance of providing cost-effective industrial equipment without compromising performance, quality or operational reliability. He noted that manufacturers in Bangladesh face increasing pressure to control production costs and remain competitive in the global market. “We are actually replacing costly European and American brands with solutions that offer comparable efficiency, quality and performance. Our industrialists need to reduce costs to maintain their competitiveness and ensure their survival in the global economy,” Sikder said. He also highlighted ISRA's longstanding partnership with KAISHAN Group, noting that the companies have worked together for approximately nine years. Sajedul Karim, Chairman of the […] The post Celio Founder and President Meet BGMEA President to Discuss Future Business Plans in Bangladesh appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Marc Grosman, Founder of renowned French fashion brand celio , along with Sebastien Bismuth, President of Celio, met BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan at the BGMEA office in Dhaka on 13 October 2026. The meeting was attended by BGMEA Directors Shah Rayeed Chowdhury and Joarder Mohammed Hosne Quamar Alam, and M. Sajedul Karim, Chairman of the Standing Committee on Trade Fair and Events. Lucie Abt, Country Manager of Celio Bangladesh, and Lorraine Gentin, Chief Transformation Officer, also attended the meeting. The discussions focused on Celio’s future business plans in Bangladesh and opportunities to strengthen collaboration with Bangladeshi suppliers. Currently, around 70% of Celio’s global sourcing comes from Bangladesh. BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan thanked Celio’s leadership for choosing Bangladesh as a reliable and strategic sourcing destination. During the meeting, the BGMEA President invited Celio’s leadership to attend the Silver Jubilee edition of BATEXPO, scheduled for 18–19 November 2026 in Dhaka. title: TrusTrace launches new report: more than one in five fashion brands selling into the U.S. have had shipments detained
summary: New research from 57 respondents across 24 countries finds only 20% hold verified data at raw material and farm level, revealing gaps in supply chain compliance readiness. The post TrusTrace launches new report: more than one in five fashion brands selling into the U.S. have had shipments detained appeared first on The Interline .
content: STOCKHOLM, Sweden, October 13, 2026 — TrusTrace, a global leader in supply chain traceability and compliance, today released The Enforcement Era: Fashion’s Compliance Readiness in Numbers , the latest in its annual industry research series. The report finds that 21% of surveyed brands selling into the U/S/ have experienced shipment detention, while 75% are not fully ready to prove material origin on demand. Launching at the Textile Exchange Conference in Vancouver, where this year’s theme, The Implementation Era , puts the focus on turning commitments into action, the report draws on primary data from 57 sustainability, compliance and supply chain leaders across 24 countries to examine brands’ current compliance practices and preparedness. Supply chain traceability used to be a sustainability initiative. In 2026, it is a trading condition. With the EUDR and PPWR coming into effect this year, the EU Forced Labor Regulation following in 2027, and Digital Product Passport (DPP) requirements on the way, the report finds that the gap between regulatory awareness and operational readiness is already having commercial consequences. content: The Better Cotton Initiative (BCI) today announced that it is now officially operating as a regenerative standard system – marking a major milestone for the world’s largest cotton sustainability scheme, which has over 20% of the world’s cotton production aligned to its standard. Building on more than 15 years of supporting locally relevant regenerative practices across cotton-growing communities, the move marks the next stage in BCI’s effort to drive healthier soils, more resilient ecosystems and stronger farmer livelihoods at scale. As the industry increasingly looks to regeneratively farmed cotton as a foundation for sustainable sourcing, BCI is helping to bridge the gap between regenerative ambitions and farming realities, ensuring that progress is driven through genuine partnership with farmers and backed by measurable outcomes. The move to a regenerative standard system reinforces farmer support through stronger requirements, targeted capacity strengthening and improved impact measurement. For retailers, brands and suppliers, it provides a reliable means of setting and meeting corporate regenerative sourcing targets, while BCI’s traceable offering opens the door to product-level claims. summary: To truly become the next stage of fashion's imaging pipeline, generative models and tools need to be able to represent and honour the product promise, and deliver a return that goes beyond the token level. The post All About AI: Matt Rouif of Photoroom appeared first on The Interline .
content: Originally released in The Interline’s AI Report 2026 , this executive interview with Photoroom is one of a 17-part series that sees The Interline quiz executives from companies who have either introduced new AI solutions or added meaningful new AI capabilities into their existing platforms . For more exclusive interviews, stories and opinions from different industry perspectives, and real survey feedback from voices from every level of fashion, download The AI Report 2026 . We’re observing a big disconnect (in both our own fashion-only data and in wider benchmarks from other sources) between the increasing capability and reliability of AI, in both a general sense and in discrete applications, and the lack of trust that end users place in its outputs. What does trust in your specific applications of AI look like, and how do you achieve and measure it? For e-commerce, trust is not really about whether an AI image looks impressive, it is about whether the product that arrives matches the expectations that image creates. Visual content shapes purchasing decisions long before a customer experiences a product firsthand, which means imagery effectively becomes the bridge between intent and transaction. When there is a significant gap between what a customer sees and what ultimately arrives, businesses feel the consequences through returns, customer dissatisfaction and, perhaps most importantly, a loss of trust that is considerably harder to recover than a single sale. summary: China has introduced new wastewater regulations requiring textile dyeing and finishing plants to demonstrate that their treated effluent does not cause unacceptable toxicity to fish embryos, marking a significant shift in environmental compliance for the country’s textile industry. The new national standard, GB 4287-2026, came into effect on 1 September 2026 for new, rebuilt and […] The post China tightens textile wastewater regulations appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: China has introduced new wastewater regulations requiring textile dyeing and finishing plants to demonstrate that their treated effluent does not cause unacceptable toxicity to fish embryos, marking a significant shift in environmental compliance for the country’s textile industry. The new national standard, GB 4287-2026, came into effect on 1 September 2026 for new, rebuilt and expanded facilities, with existing plants required to comply from 1 January 2028. It introduces fish egg toxicity testing alongside conventional chemical discharge limits, placing greater emphasis on the combined environmental impact of textile wastewater. According to Swiss textile sustainability specialist bluesign, the change represents an important development in wastewater management, moving beyond measuring individual pollutants to assessing the biological effects of treated effluent. The standard, published by China’s Ministry of Ecology and Environment and State Administration for Market Regulation in June, replaces four earlier standards covering dyeing and finishing, silk reeling, wool and hemp processing. It also extends regulatory coverage to chemical fibre weaving and industrial textile products. The new toxicity requirement applies to dyeing and finishing operations discharging treated wastewater directly into rivers, lakes or other water bodies, as well as dedicated textile industry wastewater treatment plants. Purely physical finishing operations are excluded. Under the test procedure, newly fertilised zebrafish embryos are exposed to a solution containing one part treated wastewater to five parts dilution water for 48 hours at 26°C.
