title: Bhilosa Industries proposes ₹2,500-Crore investment in Madhya Pradesh
title_ko: Bhilosa Industries는 Madhya Pradesh에 ₹2,500 Crore 투자를 제안합니다.
summary: Proposed polyester manufacturing hub at Dhar’s PM MITRA Park could create 3,750 direct jobs and strengthen the state’s man-made fibre ecosystem. Bhilosa Industries Private Limited (BIPL), one of India’s leading… The post Bhilosa Industries proposes ₹2,500-Crore investment in Madhya Pradesh appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: Proposed polyester manufacturing hub at Dhar’s PM MITRA Park could create 3,750 direct jobs and strengthen the state’s man-made fibre ecosystem. Bhilosa Industries Private Limited (BIPL), one of India’s leading polyester yarn manufacturers, has proposed a phased investment of ₹2,500 crore in Madhya Pradesh to establish an integrated polyester manufacturing facility at the PM MITRA Park in Dhar district. According to media reports, the project will begin with an initial investment of ₹2,500 crore, with commercial production targeted to commence in 2028. The proposed development is expected to generate approximately 3,750 direct employment opportunities. The company is in the final stages of selecting around 300 acres at the park, including 200 acres for textile manufacturing and another 100 acres for supporting industrial units. Building an Integrated Polyester Ecosystem The proposed facility is expected to manufacture polyester yarn, fibres, knitted fabrics and man-made fibre-based non-garment textiles. The project could also encourage the development of ancillary industries, strengthening the regional textile supply chain and creating opportunities for smaller manufacturers and suppliers. Located within the Dhar–Indore industrial belt, the proposed facility would add to Madhya Pradesh’s ambitions to develop an integrated textile manufacturing ecosystem through the PM MITRA initiative. Strengthening Bhilosa’s Manufacturing Footprint Bhilosa Industries has established a strong presence in India’s polyester value chain through continuous capacity expansion and backward and forward integration. title: BEZAKTIV Salt Advisor Enhances CHT Textile Dyes App
title_ko: BEZAKTIV Salt Advisor, CHT 섬유 염료 앱 강화
summary: New digital solution optimizes salt usage in reactive dyeing and unlocks cost-saving potential. The CHT Group continues to expand its digital service offering for textile finishers. With the new BEZAKTIV Salt Advisor, the company enhances its successful CHT Textile Dyes App with an innovative calculation tool that supports users in achieving cost-effective and resource-efficient cotton […] The post BEZAKTIV Salt Advisor Enhances CHT Textile Dyes App appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: New digital solution optimizes salt usage in reactive dyeing and unlocks cost-saving potential. The CHT Group continues to expand its digital service offering for textile finishers. With the new BEZAKTIV Salt Advisor, the company enhances its successful CHT Textile Dyes App with an innovative calculation tool that supports users in achieving cost-effective and resource-efficient cotton dyeing with BEZAKTIV reactive dyes. Over the past years, the CHT Textile Dyes App has established itself as a valuable tool for textile finishing companies. In addition to providing access to the comprehensive range of dyes and pigments offered by the CHT Group, the app includes various digital tools designed to optimize production processes while reducing water, energy, time, and operating costs. The BEZAKTIV Salt Advisor now adds another practical solution to this portfolio. In reactive cotton dyeing, salt concentration plays a crucial role. Salt increases the substantivity of the dye for the fiber, thereby increasing dye uptake. At the same time, the amount of salt used influences not only dye consumption but also overall process costs. In practice, standard tables are often used to provide general recommendations for different shade depths. However, these recommendations do not take into account the specific conditions of an individual dye recipe, leaving significant optimization potential untapped. The new BEZAKTIV Salt Advisor offers an intelligent solution to this challenge. It is based on a mathematical model developed by the CHT Group that considers the salt-dependent dye uptake behavior of all BEZAKTIV dyes under various dyeing conditions. title: Wulcea introduces graphene-heated jackets for winter wear
title_ko: Wulcea, 겨울용 그래핀 가열 재킷 출시
summary: Flexible graphene heating elements are at the centre of a new range of electrically heated jackets being introduced by New York-based apparel brand Wulcea, aimed at reducing the need for bulky winter clothing. The company’s proprietary GrapheneNano technology offers an alternative to conventional heated garments, which typically use embedded electrical wires to generate warmth. These […] The post Wulcea introduces graphene-heated jackets for winter wear appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Flexible graphene heating elements are at the centre of a new range of electrically heated jackets being introduced by New York-based apparel brand Wulcea, aimed at reducing the need for bulky winter clothing. The company’s proprietary GrapheneNano technology offers an alternative to conventional heated garments, which typically use embedded electrical wires to generate warmth. These can restrict flexibility, create uneven heating and complicate garment care. Wulcea’s new range instead incorporates flexible graphene-based heating elements designed to distribute warmth across targeted areas of the body without compromising freedom of movement. The technology uses far-infrared heating, with three adjustable temperature settings allowing wearers to control the level of warmth according to conditions and activity. The jackets can begin generating heat within three seconds and provide up to ten hours of continuous heating on the lowest setting, using an 18,400mAh rechargeable battery pack. The heating system operates at 12V and incorporates intelligent thermal control, automatically interrupting heating if internal temperatures exceed 55°C. The new collection includes hardshell jackets for outdoor work and winter sports, softshell garments for everyday use and heated vests that can be worn beneath other outerwear. The men’s hardshell jacket incorporates six heating zones positioned around the neck, upper back, lower waist and front pockets. A women’s ski jacket also features six zones, with heating extended to the upper arms as well as the neck, back and pockets. title_ko: 재활용 면화의 상업적 규모 확보
summary: Fashion for Good has launched the Cotton Reloop Matrix Project, a cross-industry initiative designed to accelerate the commercial adoption of recycled cotton by benchmarking yarn quality, recycled content and price against the requirements of fashion brands. The project brings together Fashion for Good partners Arvind, Bestseller, C&A, Interloop, Reformation and Shahi, alongside textile testing specialist […] The post Unlocking commercial scale for recycled cotton appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Fashion for Good has launched the Cotton Reloop Matrix Project, a cross-industry initiative designed to accelerate the commercial adoption of recycled cotton by benchmarking yarn quality, recycled content and price against the requirements of fashion brands. The project brings together Fashion for Good partners Arvind, Bestseller, C&A, Interloop, Reformation and Shahi, alongside textile testing specialist Uster. It aims to establish a shared, evidence-based understanding of where mechanically recycled cotton can be used commercially and how higher recycled content can be achieved without compromising product performance. Cotton accounts for approximately 19% of global fibre production but incorporating significant quantities of mechanically recycled cotton into new yarns remains challenging. During mechanical recycling, textile waste is shredded and reopened into fibres, shortening and weakening them. According to Fashion for Good, only 45–50% of the original material survives as usable fibre. The resulting shorter fibres limit the proportion of recycled cotton that can be incorporated into new yarns, with many commercial applications currently restricted to around 10% recycled content. Increasing this proportion can affect yarn strength, fabric durability and handle. Although recycling capacity is available, brands and manufacturers frequently work with fragmented testing data and differing quality specifications. Recycled cotton blends are also commonly assessed against standards developed for 100% virgin cotton, creating additional barriers to adoption. “Recycled cotton has been talked about as a scale-ready solution for years, but the industry has been working from fragmented data and siloed testing,” said Katrin Ley, Managing Director at Fashion for Good. “By plott

title: Realigning 3D And AI With Speed To Market
summary: Fashion has continued to invest in both AI and digital product creation. content: What will it take for fashion to make the leap from adopting 3D and AI as isolated disciplines, to making them part of a connected ecosystem that bridges digital and physical in a tangible way, supported by the latest academic research and ongoing technology development? Together, The Interline and Style3D evaluate whether that near-future ecosystem, properly grounded in industry knowledge and expertise, could then be able to deliver on the original promise of digital product creation by meaningfully shortening time to market – and might even begin to approach an entirely new, end-to-end promise under the umbrella of ‘physical AI’. In spite of a gloomy economic outlook, fashion hasn’t stopped scaling its investments in frontier technology. According to the industry-specific data we captured through The Interline’s 2026 survey, more than 80% of AI initiatives have accelerated in the last twelve months, and close to 70% of industry professionals expect to spend even more on AI in the coming year, across new projects and continued license and token provisions for existing ones. And AI might be the most visible category, but it’s by no means the only technology area where fashion brands are continuing to invest in the promise of digital transformation. Many of the same leading companies have also made large-scale, multi-year bets on the extended ecosystem of digital product creation. images: style3d That spend has, in many cases, delivered value in a series of standalone disciplines. content: The Lycra Company is highlighting its latest Coolmax CloakFX fibre technology at this week’s Performance Days in Munich (13-14 October), following its selection for the event’s Innovation Forum. The technology is one of just 16 innovations chosen for the curated showcase of new materials, technologies and developments. Coolmax CloakFX uses optical masking technology to diffuse light at fibre level, reducing the visibility of sweat marks while providing moisture-wicking and cooling performance. The fibre now contains 100% recycled polyester and is Global Recycled Standard (GRS) certified. “Visible sweat on apparel is a leading pain point for consumers across demographics, often forcing them to compromise between performance, comfort, and appearance,” said Tara Maurer-Mackay, Product Category Director, Branded Specialty Products, The Lycra Company. “Consumers want one fabric that does it all, and Coolmax CloakFX fibre is designed to help garments look drier while helping keep the wearer cool and dry.” The company is also presenting fabrics and garments incorporating renewable Lycra fibre, which contains 70% plant-based content and is designed to reduce the carbon footprint of apparel while maintaining the performance characteristics of conventional elastane. Among the featured developments is Set the Pace, a collaboration with Italian textile manufacturer Brugnoli and cycling apparel specialist PISSEI. The project combines Brugnoli’s patented Br4 technology and bio-based polyamide with renewable Lycra fibre to produce a technical stretch fabric containing up to 89% bio-based materials. The investment forms part of an ongoing modernisation programme at the vertically integrated company, which produces more than 60 million linear metres of […] The post One in, three out at Cedro Têxtil appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Brazilian fabric manufacturer Cedro Têxtil has been able to decommission three older stenters following the installation of a new Brückner finishing line, while also reducing natural gas consumption by more than 20%. The investment forms part of an ongoing modernisation programme at the vertically integrated company, which produces more than 60 million linear metres of fabric annually and is one of South America’s largest suppliers of workwear textiles. The new Brückner line, commissioned just over a year ago, has enabled Cedro to substantially increase production speeds while improving energy efficiency and reducing maintenance requirements. It has also delivered improvements in the finishing of super-stretch fabrics, where uniform temperature distribution and precise process control are essential to achieving consistent dimensional stability. The resulting productivity gains have enabled Cedro to consolidate production previously handled by three older stenters onto the new line, reducing the number of machines required and associated operating costs. The investment followed several years of evaluating machinery suppliers from Europe and Asia, including visits to manufacturing facilities and reference customers worldwide. The Brückner stenter SFP-4 at Cedro Têxtil © Brueckner Cedro assessed the competing technologies on productivity, maintenance requirements, energy consumption, spare parts availability and the provision of technical support in Brazil. The company ultimately selected Brückner on the basis of its combination of production performance, energy efficiency and local service capabilities. content: US yarn manufacturer Unifi is launching two new yarn technologies at Performance Days in Munich on 13-14 October, including a water-resistant yarn designed to eliminate conventional topical durable water-repellent (DWR) treatments. Resist2O Pro incorporates water resistance directly into the yarn, minimising water absorption without topical treatments or fluorinated chemistry. Compatible with different fabric formation methods, the technology could simplify textile production by eliminating a separate finishing stage. Unifi says Resist2O Pro is fluorine-free and PFOA-free, with PFOA levels below five parts per billion (ppb). Potential applications include apparel, footwear, furnishings and industrial textiles. The company’s second innovation, Cofira, combines the aesthetics and handle of spun yarns with the performance characteristics of filament yarns. It can be tailored using synthetic, blended and functional fibres to deliver different fabric properties and effects. Suitable for apparel, furnishings, equipment and accessories, Cofira can also incorporate Unifi’s existing technologies, including AMT moisture management, ChillSense cooling and ReFlexx stretch and recovery. Cofira is available globally in virgin and Repreve recycled polyester versions, including material produced using Unifi’s Repreve Takeback textile-to-textile recycling technology. Recycled versions can be traced using the company’s FiberPrint technology and are available with GRS and SCS recycled-content certification. “These new products bring multifunctional capabilities that help reduce complexities associated with high-performance products,” said Unifi CEO Eddie Ingle. title: WRAP plans new system to improve textile reuse and recycling in the UK
summary: WRAP has launched a program to redesign the UK’s textile collection, sorting, reuse and recycling systems, as rising operating losses threaten the financial viability of textile recovery. Figure: WRA...
content: WRAP has launched a program to redesign the UK’s textile collection, sorting, reuse and recycling systems, as rising operating losses threaten the financial viability of textile recovery. Figure: WRAP has launched a program to redesign the UK’s textile collection, sorting, reuse and recycling systems The UK generates an estimated 1.45 million tons of post-consumer textiles annually, equivalent to about 21 kg per person. Nearly 49% of these textiles end up in general waste or unsuitable recycling streams, limiting material recovery and increasing pressure on waste management systems. The initiative, called the Textiles Collection Transition Programme, aims to develop an industry-wide blueprint by spring 2027. Next, Primark and Tesco have provided initial funding for the program. WRAP has published its first report, Transformative Practice in Textiles Collection . It maps existing collection practices, identifies areas for improvement and outlines options to recover more textiles before they reach landfills. Sorting non-reusable textiles has become particularly difficult to sustain financially. Operators face an estimated net loss of £426 per ton because collection and sorting costs exceed the value recovered from these materials. Without structural changes, this financial pressure could shift a £400 million burden onto UK local councils by 2035. The figures highlight a key challenge for circular textiles: collecting more waste will not be enough unless the system can also finance the recovery of materials with limited resale value. Three priorities for a new collection system The first priority is to make textile disposal and donation easier for consumers. content: By K. Gopalakrishnan From a hosiery manufacturer established in 1957 to one of India’s leading branded apparel companies, Lux Industries has built its seven-decade journey around manufacturing scale, brand equity, distribution strength and consumer trust. As it enters its next phase, the company is committing ₹600 crore to nearly treble the capacity of its Dankuni manufacturing facility in West Bengal, while simultaneously investing in brands, technology, digitalisation and international expansion. Ashok Kumar Todi, Chairman Few Indian textile and apparel companies can claim a journey spanning nearly seven decades while remaining closely connected to generations of consumers. Lux Industries is one such institution. Its origins date back to 1957, when Girdhari Lal Todi established Biswanath Hosiery Mills. In 1995, Ashok Kumar Todi and Pradip Kumar Todi founded Lux Industries Limited, beginning a new phase in the evolution of the business. Over the years, Lux has evolved from a single-product, single-brand hosiery business into a diversified branded apparel enterprise spanning innerwear, outerwear, athleisure, thermal wear, rainwear and women’s apparel. Behind this evolution is a substantial manufacturing and distribution platform, with more than 44 crore garment pieces of annual production capacity across nine strategically located facilities in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh. The company’s 70-year legacy, therefore, is not merely a story of longevity. It is a story of anticipating change and investing ahead of it. content: LONDON — October 13, 2026 — North and Central American polyester filament manufacturers today announced a collective initiative, launching YarnProof powered by FibreTrace® technology. YarnProof, powered by FibreTrace, enables physical verification of regional origin at any point across the value chain, giving brands, manufacturers, and regulators increased confidence in supply chain compliance. By embedding an invisible, persistent tracer directly into polyester filament yarn during extrusion, YarnProof-enabled materials carry a verifiable origin signature that stays in the material from production through the life of the product. The FibreTrace handheld scanner detects the tracer in real time, whether in yarn, fabric, or final product. Each scan by an authorized participant creates a verification event that connects the physical material with supporting production and sourcing records. Working alongside existing documentation, YarnProof facilitates a layer of physical proof of origin to strengthen trade integrity, protect compliant supply chains, and support regional manufacturing. For YarnProof, this capability creates an additional layer of assurance supporting the yarn-forward requirements of CAFTA-DR and USMCA. North and Central American polyester filament manufacturers have united to protect the integrity of manufacturing in region. These manufacturers are: Aquafil O’Mara, Inc. CS America, Inc. CS Central America, S.A. de C.V. Nan Ya Plastics Corporation America, Premiere Fibers, LLC Skytex México, S.A. de C.V. Tecnología Textil Avanzada S.A. Textufil S.A. de C.V. Unifi Manufacturing, Inc. content: DHAKA, Oct 12, 2026 (BSS) – Batexpo 2026, the silver jubilee edition of Bangladesh’s largest international apparel exhibition, will recognise outstanding initiatives and innovations in sustainability in the garment sector through the Sustainability Leadership (TSL) Awards. The two-day exhibition will take place at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre (BCFCC) in Dhaka on November 18-19, with PDS Limited as the title sponsor, according to a press release issued by the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) here today. The TSL Awards will honour 12 initiatives across four major categories for their contributions to sustainability, technological innovation and other key areas of the apparel industry. The BGMEA will present the awards through the STILE II project of Germany- based international development organisation GIZ, in collaboration with Germany’s Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Ministry of Commerce. The Environment, Forest and Climate Change minister has agreed to attend the event as the chief guest and present the awards to the winners, the release said. The four categories are People First, Planet Positive, Next Frontier and Rising Strength. They cover initiatives in worker welfare, model factories, women’s leadership, community development, environmental sustainability, water conservation, circular textiles, business innovation, worker-centred innovation and responsible growth among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The winners will receive recognition at three levels– Platinum, Gold and Silver. summary: Italian warp knitted textiles manufacturer Pontetorto has won the Performance Days Eco Award for its innovative 6140/Biobased fleece fabric, developed using bio-based polyester fibres from Finnish company UPM. The award will be presented at Performance Days in Munich, Germany, on 13 and 14 October 2026, recognising the company’s efforts to develop lower-impact textile solutions for […] The post Pontetorto wins Performance Days Eco Award appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Italian warp knitted textiles manufacturer Pontetorto has won the Performance Days Eco Award for its innovative 6140/Biobased fleece fabric, developed using bio-based polyester fibres from Finnish company UPM. The award will be presented at Performance Days in Munich, Germany, on 13 and 14 October 2026, recognising the company’s efforts to develop lower-impact textile solutions for the outdoor, sportswear and performance apparel sectors. Founded in 1952, Pontetorto has established a strong reputation for developing technical fleece fabrics and other innovative textiles. Its latest development replaces conventional fossil-based raw materials with wood-derived bio-PET, offering an alternative to traditional polyester while maintaining the performance, comfort and technical characteristics required for demanding applications. The 6140/Biobased microfleece incorporates innovative fibres produced using raw materials derived from residues generated by the wood industry, including small branches, leaves and sawmill by-products. These resources are converted into bio-based polyester feedstocks, helping to reduce dependence on fossil-based materials. According to Pontetorto, the resulting fabric offers a lower carbon footprint than conventional polyester while retaining the functional properties expected of high-performance fleece materials. The wood used in the production process is sourced from forests certified under FSC and PEFC schemes, supporting responsible forest management and traceability throughout the supply chain. content: By Jayshri Ramani With more than four decades of polyester expertise, Jiwarajka Textile Industries is moving beyond conventional yarn manufacturing into application-driven, high-performance yarn solutions for technical textiles The global textile industry is undergoing a fundamental shift from commodity products towards materials engineered for specific performance requirements. For Jiwarajka Textile Industries, this is opening a new avenue of growth—one that builds on its more than four decades of experience in polyester yarn manufacturing while taking the company deeper into technical textiles. Anish Jiwarajka, Director, Jiwarajka Textile Industries In an exclusive interaction with The Textile Magazine , Anish Jiwarajka, Director, Jiwarajka Textile Industries, explains the company’s evolving strategy, including its expansion into Industrial Drawn Yarn (IDY), Mother Yarn, Monofilament and other specialised yarns. At the heart of the strategy is a simple change in the customer’s question—from “What is the price of this yarn?” to “What can this yarn do?” From commodity yarn to performance materials Technical textiles are fundamentally different from conventional textiles because their primary purpose is functionality rather than aesthetics or fashion. Whether it is a seat belt designed for safety, a geotextile used to strengthen infrastructure or a medical textile requiring specific protective properties, performance is the defining criterion. This is creating opportunities across automotive, infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, industrial manufacturing, safety and protection, sports and packaging. title: 뷰티 산업에 눈 돌린 대기업들…업종 경계 넘어 투자 확대
summary: 국내 뷰티 산업을 둘러싼 기업들의 투자와 사업 확장 방식이 다변화되고 있다. 식품·유통 대기업은 화장품 기업 인수를 통해 시장 진입을 추진하고, 화장품 제조기업은 의약품 유통 플랫폼과의 사업 연계를 검토하고 있다. 전통 제조 대기업의 벤처투자와 기존 뷰티 기업의 이종 산업 협업도 이어지고 있다.동원그룹은 국내 1세대 화장품 기업 참존 인수를 추진하며 뷰티 사업 진출을 검토하고 있다. 동원그룹의 식자재 유통 계열사 동원홈푸드는 지난 9월 22일 서울회생법원 관리하에 매각 절차를 밟고 있는 참존의 조건부 인수예정자로 선정됐다.인수 추진

title_ko: Lycra CloakFX를 사용하면 수분 흔적이 덜 눈에 띕니다
summary: A polyester fibre designed to make sweat marks less visible on clothing is among the technologies being highlighted by The Lycra Company at this week’s Performance Days in Munich (October 13-14). Coolmax CloakFX uses optical masking technology to diffuse light at the fibre level, reducing the visible appearance of moisture on fabrics. Rather than simply […] The post Moisture marks less visible with Lycra CloakFX appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: A polyester fibre designed to make sweat marks less visible on clothing is among the technologies being highlighted by The Lycra Company at this week’s Performance Days in Munich (October 13-14). Coolmax CloakFX uses optical masking technology to diffuse light at the fibre level, reducing the visible appearance of moisture on fabrics. Rather than simply managing perspiration, the technology aims to make garments look drier during exercise and everyday wear. The fibre, which is now made from 100% recycled polyester and is Global Recycled Standard (GRS) certified, is one of 16 products selected for the exhibition’s Innovation Forum. The technology addresses a familiar problem in sportswear, where sweat marks can remain highly visible even when fabrics are designed to transport moisture away from the skin. By incorporating the masking effect into the fibre itself, Lycra aims to reduce this visibility without compromising moisture management. Turkish textile manufacturer Ekoten will demonstrate how CloakFX can be incorporated into commercially developed fabrics and garments. Lycra will also present two collaborative projects exploring the use of bio-based and recycled materials in performance apparel. The first, Set the Pace, brings together Italian textile manufacturer Brugnoli and cycling apparel specialist Pissei in the development of a technical cycling kit containing up to 89% bio-based materials. The fabrics combine Brugnoli’s patented Br4 technology and bio-based polyamide with renewable Lycra elastane which contains 70% plant-based content. The project demonstrates how bio-based fibres can be combined in stretch fabrics designed to meet the demands of technical cycling apparel. title: Knitting and weaving a new future for green hydrogen
title_ko: 그린수소의 새로운 미래를 뜨개질하고 엮는다
summary: North Wales-based KnitMesh Technologies and German technical mesh specialist GKD are combining knitted and woven metallic structures in complete cell assemblies for hydrogen electrolysers, bringing two long-established textile technologies into the rapidly developing green hydrogen industry. The companies will jointly showcase their technologies at Hydrogen Technology World Expo in Hamburg from October 20-22, building on […] The post Knitting and weaving a new future for green hydrogen appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: North Wales-based KnitMesh Technologies and German technical mesh specialist GKD are combining knitted and woven metallic structures in complete cell assemblies for hydrogen electrolysers, bringing two long-established textile technologies into the rapidly developing green hydrogen industry. The companies will jointly showcase their technologies at Hydrogen Technology World Expo in Hamburg from October 20-22, building on a strategic partnership first announced in March 2025. For KnitMesh, the development represents a significant new application for technology it has been developing since 1957. The Greenfield, Flintshire-based company is supplying knitted wire mesh as porous transport layers (PTLs), gas diffusion layers, electrodes and elastic elements for electrolysers used to produce hydrogen. The potential of the technology has been highlighted by research from the German Aerospace Center (DLR) Institute of Engineering Thermodynamics into the performance of porous transport layers in water electrolysis. In controlled single-cell testing, DLR compared a KnitMesh knitted-wire PTL with a standard configuration and recorded a 33% increase in current density. Cell voltage was also reduced indicating lower energy requirements under the test conditions. The knitted structure further provided more uniform compression across the active area and improved gas removal while retaining electrical and thermal conductivity and permeability. “The study from DLR supports what we have found in our own development work,” said KnitMesh Technologies engineering manager Craig Jones. “Knitted wire mesh provides a unique combination of flexibility, conductivity and permeability, which can deliver significant performance improvements in electrolysis.” The findings are significant because the p

title: DPP is not a QR code, it's your factory floor's data
summary: A strategic briefing for RMG leadership: what the EU Digital Product Passport requires, where the evidence is created, and how AI-powered RFID Smart Tag-NFC captures it. Introduction Imagine a Europea...
content: A strategic briefing for RMG leadership: what the EU Digital Product Passport requires, where the evidence is created, and how AI-powered RFID Smart Tag-NFC captures it. Introduction Imagine a European shopper scanning the label on a jacket in 2028. In seconds, the label shows exactly: Its carbon footprint What it's made of, and where the materials came from Where it was produced How to care for, repair, and extend its life How to recycle or dispose of it responsibly This kind of transparency makes one thing clear: A Digital Product Passport (DPP) is not something dreamed up in a boardroom. It is built, fact by fact, on the factory floor. Bangladesh has powered global fashion for decades through scale and resilience. But the EU's Digital Product Passport is coming for our $15.54 billion export market to the EU, and it calls for a real change in how we work. Spreadsheets and manual tracking sheets can no longer protect our position. For CEOs, CFOs, General Managers, Operations and Engineering leaders , this is a defining moment. Bringing digital tracking to the factory floor through AI-powered RFID Smart Tag-NFC solutions turns compliance from a burden into a genuine competitive edge. The measurable impact is compelling: Unlock 12–18% efficiency gains at the point of production. Cut defect and rework costs by roughly 30%. Free up to 40% of staff time from manual data entry, so people can focus on analysis instead. Recover the full investment in about 11 months. These are industry-reported avg. figures — worth confirming with a pilot on your own floor before you rely on them. Rather than waiting to react to a DPP Compliance Audit , forward-looking leadership can turn this into a source of innovation. title_ko: Dutch AWARE™, 글로벌 시장에 소재 혁신을 가져오기 위해 중국 섬유 허브 Shengze와 계약 체결
summary: Government-backed traceability initiative launches as carbon-capture yarn from China is transformed into a jacket in Bangladesh with a Digital Product Passport for Europe. Dutch textile traceability company AWARE™ has signed a cooperation agreement with the Shengze Town People’s Government to develop international supply-chain traceability and help bring the region’s advanced synthetic textile innovations to global […] The post Dutch AWARE™ signs agreement with Chinese textile hub Shengze to bring material innovation to global markets appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Government-backed traceability initiative launches as carbon-capture yarn from China is transformed into a jacket in Bangladesh with a Digital Product Passport for Europe. Dutch textile traceability company AWARE™ has signed a cooperation agreement with the Shengze Town People’s Government to develop international supply-chain traceability and help bring the region’s advanced synthetic textile innovations to global markets. The agreement was announced on 10 October during the opening of the 15th Jiangsu (Shengze) Textile Expo, which also celebrated the 40th anniversary of the China Eastern Silk Market. The collaboration will establish a large-scale pilot connecting textile producers through a neutral, cross-border data infrastructure. The initiative aims to make production origin, material composition and sustainability evidence accessible to international buyers, while allowing producers to retain control of their own data. As a first step, the partners will launch the first recycled polyester Digital Product Passport. Shengze is one of China’s most important textile manufacturing centres, home to major producers including Shenghong and Hengli. The China Eastern Silk Market generates approximately RMB 200 billion in annual trading activity. From carbon-capture yarn in China to a jacket for Europe The first practical example was presented during the event. Fuhua Weaving received Wujiang District’s first carbon-capture fabric material Digital Product Passport (mDPP) label, powered by STCP first-mile traceability and AWARE™, demonstrating how innovative materials can be connected to digital production evidence. As the European Commission prepares the next EU research and innovation framework,… Read more The post EURATEX calls for a stronger textile partnership in Horizon Europe 2028–2034 appeared first on EURATEX .
content: Brussels, 6 October 2026 – EURATEX has submitted its contribution to the European Commission’s public consultation on the future European Partnerships under Horizon Europe 2028–2034, calling for the continuation of a dedicated European research and innovation partnership for the textile and clothing industry. As the European Commission prepares the next EU research and innovation framework, the future of sector-specific partnerships is under discussion. EURATEX stresses that textiles must remain a strategic priority , ensuring that European companies, particularly SMEs, can access the research, technologies and funding needed to strengthen their competitiveness. The European textile and clothing industry generates €166 billion in annual turnover and employs 1.2 million people across approximately 194,000 companies. With 99.8% of businesses being SMEs, dedicated European cooperation is essential to translate research into practical industrial solutions. Keeping Textiles of the Future at the heart of European innovation EURATEX calls for the continuation and reinforcement of Textiles of the Future , the co-programmed European Partnership launched under Horizon Europe’s 2025–2027 Strategic Plan. The partnership connects companies, research organisations and technology providers to address common industrial challenges. It is expected to mobilise at least €60 million in its initial phase, with projects running until 2030. Discontinuing the partnership after 2027 would risk interrupting this momentum before its first projects have delivered their full results. content: NUB Textile Club successfully organized a programme titled “Mastering the Art of Presentation” at Northern University Bangladesh (NUB), aiming to enhance students’ presentation skills, communication abilities, and confidence. The programme featured Sabbir Sarker, Founder of EnglishA2Z , as the guest speaker. He shared valuable insights, practical experiences, and effective techniques for delivering impactful presentations, emphasizing the importance of clear communication and confident delivery. Manindra Nath Roy, Assistant Professor, Department of Textile Engineering, Northern University Bangladesh (NUB), was also present at the programme and shared valuable insights and guidance with the participants. The initiative was organized in collaboration with NextGen Youth Society , whose support and cooperation contributed to the successful execution of the programme. The programme provided students with an opportunity to develop their presentation and communication skills, which are essential for academic and professional growth. The organizers expressed their gratitude to the speakers, participants, collaborators, and everyone involved in making the event successful. Through such initiatives, NUB Textile Club continues to encourage students to develop essential professional skills and prepare for future career opportunities. title: BATEXPO 2026 to honor sustainable initiatives in apparel sector with Sustainability Leadership (TSL) Award
summary: On 18–19 November 2026, Bangladesh’s largest international apparel exhibition, BATEXPO 2026 (Silver Jubilee Edition), will be held at the Bangladesh–China Friendship Conference Center. PDS Limited is...
content: On 18–19 November 2026, Bangladesh’s largest international apparel exhibition, BATEXPO 2026 (Silver Jubilee Edition), will be held at the Bangladesh–China Friendship Conference Center. PDS Limited is the title sponsor of this mega event. One of the key highlights of BATEXPO 2026 will be the prestigious Sustainability Leadership (TSL) Award, honoring outstanding contributions in sustainability, technological innovation, and other critical areas. The award will be presented by the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), through the Germany-based international development organization GIZ’s “Stile II” project, with support from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Ministry of Commerce. A total of 12 initiatives across 4 categories will be recognized. The Hon’ble Minister of Environment and Climate Change has kindly consented to attend as Chief Guest and present the awards to the winners. The 4 Award Categories: People First: Worker welfare, model factories, women in leadership, and community champions. Planet Positive: Sustainability Leader of the Year, Water Guardian, and Circular Textile Pioneer. Next Frontier : Business Innovator of the Year, Future-Ready Award, and Worker-Centric Innovation. Rising Strength: Small Factory Big Impact, Resourceful Innovation, and Growing Responsibly Award (for SMEs). Winners will be honored at three levels: Platinum, Gold, and Silver. content: Bangladesh’s Mongla Export Processing Zone (EPZ) is adding another export-oriented garment manufacturer. Chinese company Longteng Garment Co Ltd plans to establish a $17 million factory, strengthening the zone’s industrial base and employment potential. The proposed factory in Bagerhat will manufacture underwear and bras, with an annual production capacity of 6 million pieces. The project is expected to create jobs for 3,005 Bangladeshi nationals, according to the Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA). The investment also reflects the potential to expand Bangladesh’s role in the global intimate apparel supply chain. Longteng plans to produce for international brands including Aerie, Calvin Klein, Zara, Florence & Fred (Tesco), ASOS and Primark, with major buyers including H&M, Walmart, Marks & Spencer and Gap. The company intends to export its products to markets across North America, Europe, Asia, South America, Africa and Australia, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, Canada, Brazil and Australia. Md Tanvir Hossain, Member (Investment Promotion) of BEPZA, and Lin Qiangqiang, Chairman of Longteng Garment Co Ltd, signed the investment agreement at the BEPZA Complex in Dhaka on Monday. BEPZA Executive Chairman Major General Mohammad Moazzem Hossain attended the ceremony and assured the investor of the authority’s support in establishing and operating the factory. The project comes as Mongla EPZ continues to build its industrial and export base. As of September 2026, 39 enterprises were operating in the zone, while another 10 were at the implementation stage. summary: Barmag’s new Wings POY 2.0 1920/16 winding concept increases the number of winding positions from 12 to 16, enabling polyester spinning plants to achieve up to 33% higher production density. For Georg Strausberg, however, the more important development is the automation needed to sustain this increased output without compromising process stability, yarn quality or operating […] The post Barmag puts repeatability at the heart of productivity appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Barmag’s new Wings POY 2.0 1920/16 winding concept increases the number of winding positions from 12 to 16, enabling polyester spinning plants to achieve up to 33% higher production density. For Georg Strausberg, however, the more important development is the automation needed to sustain this increased output without compromising process stability, yarn quality or operating efficiency. Speaking at the recent Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress, Strausberg emphasised that the objective of automation should not simply be to introduce additional functions, robots or more sophisticated machinery, but to eliminate the variability that can undermine production performance. “The real question is not how to achieve higher productivity once but how to achieve it every day,” he said. “This is where automation becomes decisive.” The distinction is particularly relevant to polyester filament production, where higher production density places additional demands on process control, yarn handling and operating personnel. “If higher productivity leads to more breaks, more waste, greater operator dependency, or less stable quality, it is not real progress,” Strausberg said. Redesigning the process First introduced to a selected audience at ITMA Asia + CITME 2025 in Singapore, POY 2.0 represents a redesign of Barmag’s production technology for partially oriented yarn, covering the entire process from spinning and filament cooling through to winding and digital monitoring. Rather than concentrating solely on increasing winding capacity, Barmag has modified several core components to improve their combined performance. title: Polartec® Introduces The Next Generation Of Polartec Alpha™ Active Insulation
title_ko: Polartec®, 차세대 Polartec Alpha™ 활성 단열재 출시
summary: SPARTANBURG, S.C. — October 13, 2026 — Polartec®, a Milliken & Company brand and global supplier of innovative performance textiles, introduces the next generation of Polartec Alpha™ active insulation, featuring a new patent-pending construction engineered to deliver greater durability and design versatility while preserving the breathability and dynamic thermoregulation that has made Alpha a benchmark […]
content: SPARTANBURG, S.C. — October 13, 2026 — Polartec®, a Milliken & Company brand and global supplier of innovative performance textiles, introduces the next generation of Polartec Alpha active insulation, featuring a new patent-pending construction engineered to deliver greater durability and design versatility while preserving the breathability and dynamic thermoregulation that has made Alpha a benchmark for active insulation. Polartec Alpha was born from an unusually complex performance challenge: create insulation for highly active military users who move rapidly between periods of intense exertion and lower activity in cold environments. Traditional insulation could provide warmth, but often at the expense of breathability and moisture management as activity increased. Polartec Alpha approached the problem differently. Its open, highly breathable construction was engineered to balance insulation with airflow, helping manage excess heat and moisture as exertion and environmental conditions change. That combination helped establish Polartec Alpha within military and special operations communities around the world and ultimately helped create an entirely new category of active insulation. Over the following decade, the same performance principle moved into outdoor, endurance and lifestyle apparel. Polartec Alpha became known for its combination of lightweight warmth, exceptional breathability, fast drying, and packability – forever changing how designers approached insulation for people in motion. Now, Polartec is advancing the platform once again. At the center of the next generation is a patent-pending construction engineered to improve the structural integrity of the fabric while maintaining the open architecture fundamental to Polartec Alpha performance. summary: Italian warp-knitted fabric specialist Eurojersey and Portuguese technical apparel manufacturer Petratex have joined forces to develop Optical Motion, a new performance wear project that integrates textile innovation, garment engineering and advanced manufacturing from the earliest stages of product development. Using cycling as its starting point, the collaboration explores how fabrics, garment construction and technologies can […] The post Eurojersey and Petratex take new approach to performance appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Italian warp-knitted fabric specialist Eurojersey and Portuguese technical apparel manufacturer Petratex have joined forces to develop Optical Motion, a new performance wear project that integrates textile innovation, garment engineering and advanced manufacturing from the earliest stages of product development. Using cycling as its starting point, the collaboration explores how fabrics, garment construction and technologies can be developed together to optimise aerodynamics, comfort, breathability and freedom of movement. The project, developed under the concept ‘Engineered Together’, combines Eurojersey’s expertise in technical warp-knitted fabrics with Petratex’s capabilities in garment design, engineering and production. Rather than treating fabric and garment development as separate processes, the partners have created an integrated approach in which material selection, construction and fit are developed simultaneously. Optical Motion incorporates different textile structures positioned according to the demands of the body and movement. Mesh fabrics enhance ventilation, structured surfaces are designed to improve aerodynamics, while high-density materials provide support and stability. The resulting garments are engineered to maintain comfort and performance over long distances. © Eurojersey The capsule also features a distinctive visual identity inspired by Op Art, using three-dimensional textures, contrasting surfaces and reflective elements to create a sense of movement and speed. These aesthetic features are developed alongside the technical characteristics of the garments rather than added during the final design stages. summary: GREENSBORO, N.C. — October 13, 2026 — Unifi, Inc., together with polyester filament yarn manufacturers across North and Central America, today announced the launch of YarnProof™, an industry-wide initiative designed to provide immediate, physical verification of polyester filament yarn origin throughout the supply chain. YarnProof, powered by FibreTrace® technology, embeds an invisible and permanent tracer […]
content: GREENSBORO, N.C. — October 13, 2026 — Unifi, Inc., together with polyester filament yarn manufacturers across North and Central America, today announced the launch of YarnProof , an industry-wide initiative designed to provide immediate, physical verification of polyester filament yarn origin throughout the supply chain. YarnProof, powered by FibreTrace® technology, embeds an invisible and permanent tracer into polyester filament yarn during extrusion. The tracer remains with the material throughout its lifecycle and can be immediately detected using a proprietary FibreTrace handheld scanner at designated points across the supply chain, including yarn, fabric, and finished goods. By linking physical verification to origin claims, YarnProof supports compliance with the yarn-forward requirements of the CAFTA-DR and USMCA trade agreements. Working alongside existing documentation and certification systems, YarnProof adds a layer of verifiable evidence that strengthens trade integrity, protects compliant supply chains, and supports regional manufacturing. “Supply chain integrity is a top priority for our brand,” said Nick Pence, Senior Director of Material Supply at Under Armour. “As we continue to rely on yarn manufacturers in the region to fulfill our brand’s strategic goals, we are encouraged by the proactive steps the industry is taking to enhance transparency and reliability throughout the supply chain, and to provide physical evidence to support sourcing history.” As concerns over non-compliant trade continue to grow, trade regulators like U.S. Customs and Border Protection have emphasized the importance of private-sector solutions that help strengthen supply chain traceability and support enforcement efforts. “Traditional methods of fraud detection, such as document

The organiser says its latest developments reflect a strategy to strengthen international connections, encourage innovation and provide greater value to the global fashion […] The post Munich Fabric Start expands digital reach appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Munich Fabric Start is expanding its role beyond the traditional trade fair calendar with a year-round digital platform, new industry partnerships and a government-backed initiative supporting emerging German textile and fashion businesses. The organiser says its latest developments reflect a strategy to strengthen international connections, encourage innovation and provide greater value to the global fashion and textile industry between its twice-yearly exhibitions in Munich. Central to the strategy is the launch of 365 Days Munich Fabric Start, a digital platform building on the organiser’s 30th anniversary campaign, 30 Years. 30 Stories. The initiative will provide year-round industry insights, emerging trends and perspectives through podcasts, editorial content, video and an expanded social media presence. The platform is designed to extend industry dialogue beyond the physical exhibitions, creating additional opportunities for knowledge exchange, networking and collaboration across the international textile supply chain. A further development is a partnership with Future Fashion Assembly, beginning with an industry webinar entitled What Comes Next for European Fashion Supply? on 28 October 2026. Bringing together brands, retailers, textile manufacturers and specialists in sourcing, technology and innovation, the webinar will examine practical solutions for improving the competitiveness of European fashion supply chains. Discussions will focus on the commercial benefits of artificial intelligence and digitalisation, preparations for Digital Product Passports, compliance with sustainability claims legislation and the implications of evolving EU regulations. content: ₹344-crore spinning expansion completed, weaving capacity to rise to 65 million metres; company sharpens focus on asset utilisation, circularity, seamless garments and capital efficiency Sangam (India) Limited is entering a new phase of its growth journey. After several years of investment and capacity creation, the integrated textile manufacturer is now shifting its focus from project execution to operational excellence , with the objective of extracting higher returns from the assets already deployed. R. P. Soni, Chairman The company’s consolidated revenue from operations rose 13.22% to ₹3,234.53 crore in FY2025-26 , from ₹2,856.95 crore in the previous year. This performance comes as Sangam completes or advances a series of strategic investments spanning spinning, weaving, recycled polyester and downstream textile and apparel businesses. Chairman R. P. Soni describes the transition as more than a change in operational priorities. Having moved from a phase of adding capacity to one focused on making every spindle and loom contribute to the bottom line, Sangam is now seeking to build a self-sustaining model of high-yield growth. The strategy is centred on three broad priorities: improving utilisation of existing assets, increasing value addition and strengthening financial efficiency. Building scale across the textile value chain Sangam has developed an integrated textile platform extending from fibre and yarn manufacturing to weaving, processing, denim and garments. The company’s portfolio includes grey yarn, cotton blends, PV dyed yarn, denim, knitted fabrics, woven and processed fabrics and garments. In an exclusive interview at TITAS 2026, CEO Mr. Florian Finke discusses the company’s expanding technological capabilities, opportunities in technical textiles and its growing ambitions for the Indian market. BY Nithin Kumar H A fabric defect identified during inspection can still become an expensive production problem if the information never reaches the cutting room. The fabric may be inspected, graded and approved for production, yet the precise location of an imperfection can remain disconnected from the marker and spreading plan. By the time it is discovered on a cut component, the opportunity to address it efficiently may already have passed. title: New EU chemical limits add compliance pressure for apparel exporters
summary: New European Union (EU) restrictions on PFHxA in clothing, accessories, and footwear took effect on October 10, 2026. The rules set strict limits on the chemical, adding another compliance requirement...
content: New European Union (EU) restrictions on PFHxA in clothing, accessories, and footwear took effect on October 10, 2026. The rules set strict limits on the chemical, adding another compliance requirement for apparel brands and their suppliers. The regulation covers undecafluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA). It restricts products containing PFHxA and its salts at or above 25 parts per billion (ppb) and related substances at or above 1,000 ppb, measured in homogeneous material. The new rules apply to clothing, related accessories and footwear for the general public. Certain personal protective equipment, medical devices and construction textiles are exempt. Products placed on the market before October 10, 2026, are also covered by a transitional exemption under the regulation. The restriction is part of a wider effort to reduce the release of persistent chemicals into the environment. However, differing chemical restrictions across markets can make compliance more complex for brands sourcing products from multiple countries. For Bangladesh’s apparel industry, the rules highlight the importance of chemical management across the supply chain. Exporters serving EU buyers may need to review chemical inputs, check supplier declarations, and maintain reliable test records to demonstrate compliance with applicable requirements. The EU regulation also sets a separate deadline for textiles, leather, and similar materials used in other consumer products. Restrictions on these materials, excluding clothing and related accessories already covered, will apply from October 10, 2027.

title: Unifi moves water resistance into the yarn
title_ko: Unifi는 방수 기능을 원사로 옮깁니다.
summary: Unifi is moving water resistance from the finishing stage into the yarn itself with a new technology designed to eliminate the need for conventional topical durable water-repellent (DWR) treatments. The US manufacturer will introduce Resist2O Pro alongside a second new yarn technology, Cofira, at Performance Days in Munich this week (October 13-14). Resist2O Pro is […] The post Unifi moves water resistance into the yarn appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Unifi is moving water resistance from the finishing stage into the yarn itself with a new technology designed to eliminate the need for conventional topical durable water-repellent (DWR) treatments. The US manufacturer will introduce Resist2O Pro alongside a second new yarn technology, Cofira, at Performance Days in Munich this week (October 13-14). Resist2O Pro is engineered to minimise water absorption without the use of topical treatments or fluorinated chemistry and can be employed with different methods of fabric formation. This potentially gives textile manufacturers greater flexibility in developing water-resistant fabrics while removing a separate finishing treatment from the production process. Unifi says the technology is fluorine-free and PFOA-free – defined as containing less than 5 ppb (parts per billion) – and is targeting applications ranging from apparel and footwear to furnishings and industrial textiles. The company is also launching Cofira, a yarn designed to combine characteristics normally associated with spun and filament constructions. Cofira has been developed to provide the aesthetics and handle of a spun yarn while retaining the performance characteristics available from filament yarns. It can be tailored using synthetic, blended and functional fibre technologies to create different fabric properties and effects. Potential applications include apparel, furnishings, equipment and accessories, and the yarn can also be combined with existing Unifi technologies including AMT (moisture management), ChillSense (cool-to-the-touch properties) and ReFlexx (stretch and recovery). title_ko: 규제에서 옷이 어떻게 사용되는지 고려해야 하는 이유
summary: By the International Wool Textile Organisation BRUSSELS – A garment can pass demanding strength tests and still be worn only a handful of times. It may fit badly, feel uncomfortable or no longer be considered ‘current’. Put another way, a strong fabric offers limited benefit if the garment made from it spends most of its [...] The post Why regulations need to consider how clothes are used appeared first on Apparel Insider .
content: By the International Wool Textile Organisation BRUSSELS – A garment can pass demanding strength tests and still be worn only a handful of times. It may fit badly, feel uncomfortable or no longer be considered ‘current’. Put another way, a strong fabric offers limited benefit if the garment made from it spends most of its life unworn. Understanding this gap is essential if Europe’s textile policies are to deliver the environmental benefits they promise. At the International Wool Textile Organisation, we believe the development of EU textile rules needs to give much greater weight to what happens to clothing in everyday life. While physical testing provides useful evidence about a garment’s ability to withstand use, it cannot, on its own, establish how much use that garment will receive. Extrinsic durability Researchers describe these wider influences on continued use as “extrinsic durability.” The term, which has become increasingly prevalent in recent years, covers considerations all of us will be familiar with. These include whether clothing fits, whether people enjoy wearing it, how they value it and whether it remains relevant as their lives change. The evidence to support the concept of extrinsic durability can be found in a review by researchers at Oslo Metropolitan University which drew together 17 studies of clothing disposal. Excluding other or unknown reasons, physical quality accounted for 37 per cent of disposal motivations, fit for 28 per cent and perceived value for 35 per cent. These findings do not suggest that quality is unimportant, but they do show how much a policy based predominantly (or only) on physical performance would miss. content: Luxury knitwear manufacturer John Smedley has partnered with historic Yorkshire woollen mill Abraham Moon & Sons (MOON) to launch a limited-edition collection of knitwear and homeware, bringing together more than four centuries of combined British textile manufacturing expertise. Launched on 8 October 2026, the John Smedley x MOON collection marks the first capsule in a planned long-term partnership between the two heritage brands. Combining John Smedley’s fine knitwear expertise with MOON’s woollen textile manufacturing capabilities, the collaboration celebrates the versatility, durability and enduring appeal of wool. © John Smedley The collection also represents John Smedley’s first venture into homewares, extending the brand’s established knitwear offering into interior textiles. Featuring woollen throws, cushions, a chunky knit and a woollen hat, the range combines traditional textile craftsmanship with contemporary styling. A colour palette of ginger, grey, cream and midnight blue is complemented by variegated stripes and plain textures, reflecting the growing interest in natural materials and timeless interior design. John Smedley CEO Jess Mcguire-Dudley said the partnership was a natural extension of the companies’ shared manufacturing heritage and commitment to quality. “John Smedley and MOON share generations of specialist knowledge, British manufacturing, and a belief in creating beautiful products that are made to last. title: Lenzing expands denim network with new Japanese collection
title_ko: Lenzing, 새로운 일본 컬렉션으로 데님 네트워크 확장
summary: The Remod collection, to be introduced at Kingpins Amsterdam this week (October 14-15), explores how three different types of Tencel Lyocell fibre can be used to create contrasting denim textures, weights and finishes, including constructions containing no cotton. The fabrics have been woven at Kaihara’s vertically integrated mill in Hiroshima, building on a relationship with […] The post Lenzing expands denim network with new Japanese collection appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: The Remod collection, to be introduced at Kingpins Amsterdam this week (October 14-15), explores how three different types of Tencel Lyocell fibre can be used to create contrasting denim textures, weights and finishes, including constructions containing no cotton. The fabrics have been woven at Kaihara’s vertically integrated mill in Hiroshima, building on a relationship with Lenzing that dates back to the 1990s. The collection includes heavyweight men’s jackets, mid-weight wide-leg and stretch jeans and casual shirting. It combines conventional denim manufacturing techniques with different fibre blends to achieve specific fabric characteristics. Central to the development is Tencel Lyocell HV100, first introduced at Kingpins Amsterdam in October 2025 as a cotton-like alternative to standard lyocell fibres. The fibre employs Lenzing’s Variocut technology to introduce controlled variations in fibre length, creating the subtle irregularities and more opaque, matte appearance associated with cotton denim. A second fibre, Tencel Lyocell dtex 2.2, has a coarser structure and a fibre length of 51mm. It produces a drier, stiffer handle and natural slub effects resembling linen, adding body and structure to fabrics without significantly increasing weight. Standard Tencel Lyocell, meanwhile, contributes softness, drape and colour depth. title: Orientation Program Held for 5th Batch Students at Jamalpur Textile Institute
summary: The orientation program for the new students of the 5th batch of the 2026-27 academic year was held at Jamalpur Textile Institute (JTI). The JTI family organized the program in the institute auditorium. A.N.M. Tarikul Islam, Director (Joint Secretary), Administration and Finance, Department of Textiles, attended as chief guest. Engineer Md. Saifur Rahman, Deputy Director […] The post Orientation Program Held for 5th Batch Students at Jamalpur Textile Institute appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: The orientation program for the new students of the 5th batch of the 2026-27 academic year was held at Jamalpur Textile Institute (JTI). The JTI family organized the program in the institute auditorium. A.N.M. Tarikul Islam, Director (Joint Secretary), Administration and Finance, Department of Textiles, attended as chief guest. Engineer Md. Saifur Rahman, Deputy Director (Administration), Department of Textiles, attended as special guest. Principal Engineer A.K.M. Monjurul Haque presided over the program. Instructors Engineer Kamal Hossain, Aminul Islam, Jesmin Akter, Rashedujjaman, Mahfuzur Rahman and Subal Chandra Debnath, along with all other instructors and staff of the institute, were also present. Members of the Jamalpur Textile Institute Rover Scout Group volunteered to ensure the orientation ran smoothly and in an orderly manner. They guided the new students and assisted in various activities. The organizers expressed hope that this event, combining education, friendship, sports and mutual harmony, would inspire the new students on their journey ahead. title: Astronauts chose the Stryke: An Ashulia factory has been making it for years
summary: When NASA’s Artemis II crew travelled farther from Earth than any humans before them, viewers spotted a familiar cargo pant: the 5.11 Stryke. In Ashulia, Ananta Garments sews that very design for the...
content: When NASA’s Artemis II crew travelled farther from Earth than any humans before them, viewers spotted a familiar cargo pant: the 5.11 Stryke. In Ashulia, Ananta Garments sews that very design for the brand, in a country that makes more of 5.11’s gear than any other. A moon mission. A technical cargo pant. An unexpected Bangladesh connection: Ananta Companies. AT 6.35 IN THE evening, Florida time, on 1 April 2026, NASA’s Space Launch System rose from Launch Pad 39B at the Kennedy Space Center on 8.8 million pounds of thrust. Strapped inside the Orion capsule, which they had named Integrity, were four astronauts: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen. They were the first people to set out for the Moon in more than half a century. As per NASA’s mission account, Integrity swung around the Moon five days later, passing about 6,500 kilometers above its surface. At the farthest point of the voyage the crew was nearly 407,000 kilometers from home, farther from Earth than any human beings had ever been, breaking a record the crew of Apollo 13 had held since 1970. By the time the capsule splashed into the Pacific off San Diego on 10 April, it had covered more than 1.1 million kilometers. Millions of people followed the mission as it happened. And in that flood of images, a handful of viewers noticed something nobody had expected to talk about. It was not a spacesuit, nor a control panel, nor the Earth hanging in the capsule window. It was a pair of trousers. The sleuths and the stitch The clues were modest. summary: SALTSJÖ-BOO, Sweden — October 12, 2026 — “Bringing Calvin into Cyclothe marks our deliberate transition from developing infrastructure to deploying it commercially at industrial scale. content: SALTSJÖ-BOO, Sweden — October 12, 2026 — “Bringing Calvin into Cyclothe marks our deliberate transition from developing infrastructure to deploying it commercially at industrial scale. His deep command of the global textile value chain, global brand dynamics, and supply chain transformation gives us the exact leadership required to navigate this next phase,” says Halit Kosmaz, Founder of Cyclothe. Calvin Woolley Cyclothe, the Swedish circular technology company, enters its next phase of commercial growth with the appointment of Calvin Woolley, former Sustainable Business Manager for Textiles at IKEA, as Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer. Extensive industry experience With more than 25 years of international textile industry leadership, including 15 years driving global textile sustainability and circularity initiatives at Inter IKEA, Calvin Woolley brings an intimate understanding of end-to-end supply chains, enterprise brand requirements, and the structural friction that has historically prevented circular systems from scaling. “It is clear that the textile sector does not suffer from a lack of circular ambition. It suffers from a lack of functioning infrastructure. What we’re missing is an infrastructure capable of managing new legislation in a commercially viable way—an infrastructure where measurable, high-value reverse flows can actually be built at scale. Cyclothe is building that exact missing layer, linking people, products, cities, brands, and recyclers through one connected, intelligent system,” says Calvin Woolley. Smart infrastructure system for circular solutions The appointment of Calvin Woolley marks an intentional shift as Cyclothe moves from proprietary technology development to widespread commercial deployment. title: Billion Rise expands manufacturing in Vietnam
summary: Billion Rise Knitting, a leading vertically integrated manufacturer of knitted fabrics for sportswear, activewear, swimwear and intimate apparel, has opened a new manufacturing facility in Thanh Hoa, Vietnam, as part of a US$100 million investment to expand its global production capabilities. The new factory will complement the company’s established manufacturing operations in Qingyuan, China, providing […] The post Billion Rise expands manufacturing in Vietnam appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Billion Rise Knitting, a leading vertically integrated manufacturer of knitted fabrics for sportswear, activewear, swimwear and intimate apparel, has opened a new manufacturing facility in Thanh Hoa, Vietnam, as part of a US$100 million investment to expand its global production capabilities. The new factory will complement the company’s established manufacturing operations in Qingyuan, China, providing international apparel brands with greater sourcing flexibility and access to advanced knitting, dyeing, printing and finishing technologies. Developed in three phases, the Vietnam facility will eventually cover approximately 320,000 square metres and is expected to achieve an annual production capacity of up to 100 million metres of fabric. The first phase, comprising approximately 110,000 square metres, has been completed. Additional knitting, dyeing and printing capacity will be introduced during the second phase, scheduled for completion in the third quarter of 2027, with the final phase expected to be completed in the third quarter of 2029. “We’re pleased to give our customers greater sourcing flexibility with the addition of our Vietnam operation to our established manufacturing base in Qingyuan, China,” said Charles Chen, CEO and owner of Billion Rise. © Billion Rise Knitting “After a decade of investment in developing the facility and building it to the same high standards our customers expect from us, we’re confident Vietnam will deliver the quality, technical expertise and consistency our brand partners require.” The new operation is being developed with manufacturing capabilities comparable to Billion Rise’s Chinese facility, including warp and weft knitting, dyeing, digital printing, flat-bed printing, heat-transfer printing, stentering and finishing. title: Livinguard cuts reactive dyeing wash-off time
title_ko: 리빙가드, 반응성 염색 워시오프 시간 단축
summary: Swiss textile technology company Livinguard has demonstrated how its +DYE SC after-treatment can reduce the conventional nine-stage wash-off process following reactive dyeing of cotton to just six steps, cutting water consumption by 32% and processing time by 23%. The results come from an independent assessment commissioned by Fashion for Good and conducted by technical consultancy […] The post Livinguard cuts reactive dyeing wash-off time appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Swiss textile technology company Livinguard has demonstrated how its +DYE SC after-treatment can reduce the conventional nine-stage wash-off process following reactive dyeing of cotton to just six steps, cutting water consumption by 32% and processing time by 23%. The results come from an independent assessment commissioned by Fashion for Good and conducted by technical consultancy BluWin at a knitwear processing mill in India. Steam consumption was reduced by up to 88%, while calculated greenhouse gas emissions fell by 29%. Crucially, the simplified process was achieved using existing dyeing equipment, recipes and dyestuffs, without machinery modifications. Wash-off challenge The reactive dyeing of cotton and other cellulosic fibres requires extensive washing and soaping after dye application to remove hydrolysed dyes that have not bonded permanently with the fibres. These processes are often carried out at high temperatures and account for a substantial proportion of the water and energy consumed during dyeing. Livinguard +DYE SC addresses this problem through a cationic after-treatment that binds to both the fibre and hydrolysed dye, forming a charged, crosslinked network that restricts dye release during subsequent washing. This allows the conventional wash-off sequence to be shortened considerably while maintaining the required colour fastness. In the Indian trial, the mill’s existing nine-stage process, which included two soaping baths at 95°C and hot washes at 80°C and 90°C, was reduced to six stages incorporating a single warm wash at 60°C. Water consumption during wash-off fell from 37.44 to 25.33 litres per kilogram of fabric, while processing time decreased from 5.72 to 4.42 hours. title: Arclin Introduces Kevlar® EXO™ XP E480
title_ko: Arclin, Kevlar® EXO™ XP E480 출시
summary: ALPHARETTA, Ga. — October 12, 2026 — Arclin, a materials science company, today announced the launch of Kevlar® EXO™ XP E480, the latest innovation in its personal protection portfolio. Combining the proven ballistic and trauma-reduction performance of Kevlar® XP technology with the advanced capabilities of Kevlar® EXO™ fiber, the new solution enables body armor manufacturers […]
content: ALPHARETTA, Ga. — October 12, 2026 — Arclin, a materials science company, today announced the launch of Kevlar® EXO XP E480, the latest innovation in its personal protection portfolio. Combining the proven ballistic and trauma-reduction performance of Kevlar® XP technology with the advanced capabilities of Kevlar® EXO fiber, the new solution enables body armor manufacturers to achieve significantly lighter weight while meeting NIJ Level IIIA/HG2 protection requirements, helping improve wearer comfort, mobility, and operational effectiveness. “Protective equipment is only effective if users can wear it comfortably throughout their entire mission,” said Joe Hovanec, Arclin’s Vice President of Kevlar® EXO . “With Kevlar® EXO XP E480, manufacturers can achieve armor that is up to 25% lighter and provides up to 40% greater comfort*, helping reduce fatigue while maintaining the trusted protection users depend on.” Engineered to perform in demanding field conditions, Kevlar® EXO XP E480 combines high stopping power, excellent bullet-flattening performance, and exceptional durability in a lighter-weight construction. The material’s unique fiber architecture also helps reduce layer counts and stitching requirements, enabling streamlined armor designs and potentially lowering manufacturing complexity and labor costs. Kevlar® EXO XP E480 is now available for evaluation to customers worldwide. To learn more, visit XPE480 – Arclin. *vs. XP K520 for level IIIA/HG2 NIJ. Kevlar® and Kevlar® EXO are registered trademarks of Arclin. Posted: October 12, 2026 Source: Arclin

Rubel Miah, Managing Director of Sixem Fashion, was appointed Convenor, while S M Sumon Bappy, Managing […] The post Bangladesh Mini Garments Manufacturers Association Forms Convening Committee and Discusses Future Plans appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Mini garments entrepreneurs met on Friday, 9 October 2026, at Hotel Platinum in Banani, Dhaka. The meeting focused on forming the convening committee of the Bangladesh Mini Garments Manufacturers Association and discussing future initiatives to develop the sector. Md. Rubel Miah, Managing Director of Sixem Fashion, was appointed Convenor, while S M Sumon Bappy, Managing Director of Sordar Garments, was appointed Member Secretary. The other representatives included in the committee were designated as Members. Participants emphasized developing the mini garments sector through training, skills enhancement, knowledge and experience sharing, and stronger cooperation among entrepreneurs. Participants also discussed plans to develop an association website to facilitate communication, information sharing, and connections among members. The discussion also covered improvements in production practices, product quality and business management, along with new market opportunities and possible solutions to common challenges faced by mini garments manufacturers. Participants expressed their commitment to working together to develop the sector. After forming the convening committee and discussing future plans, the meeting concluded with a cake-cutting ceremony.
