content: The Hong Kong Research Institute of Textiles and Apparel (HKRITA) celebrated its 20th anniversary with an Innovation and Technology Symposium at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre on 9 October 2026, bringing together government, academic and industry leaders to explore the future of textile innovation and sustainable development. Held under the theme ‘Weaving 20 Years | Threading New Paths. Building to Last’, the event highlighted HKRITA’s achievements in applied research, technology transfer and commercialisation, while examining emerging opportunities in artificial intelligence, green innovation, circularity and talent development. A key highlight was the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between HKRITA and Ocean Park Corporation to strengthen collaboration in sustainability, innovation, education and knowledge exchange. The partnership will explore opportunities in green technology and circular economy initiatives, combining HKRITA’s research expertise with Ocean Park’s conservation, education and public engagement capabilities. In her welcome address, HKRITA Chairman Teresa Yang emphasised the growing importance of innovation in maintaining industrial competitiveness and supporting sustainable development. “Innovation and technology are reshaping industries at an unprecedented pace. Amid growing global competition and sustainability challenges, innovation is no longer an option, but a key driver of industrial upgrading and long-term value creation,” she said. content: Al-Razi Chemical Complex Limited, a subsidiary of Smart Group of Industries, is strengthening its position as a local textile chemical manufacturer with a growing focus on product consistency, technical support, responsible chemical management and international standards. Bangladesh remains its main market, while its products are also exporting to several regional textile manufacturing countries. As buyer expectations increasingly emphasize safer chemistry, traceability and environmental performance, Al-Razi is aligning its operations accordingly. Its recent engagement as a bluesign® system partner marks an important step in this journey. content: Archroma and Nicca Chemical are collaborating to support the continued growth of ZELAN™ non-fluorinated durable water repellents (DWRs) across the global textile industry. The announcement follows Nicca’s acquisition of the ZELAN™ business from The Chemours Company in March 2026 and extends Archroma’s decade-long legacy with the ZELAN™ brand. Archroma’s role as ZELAN™’s global distribution, marketing and technical support partner dates to the 2015 launch of Teflon EcoElite™ with ZELAN™ R3 by Chemours and Huntsman Textile Effects, which Archroma acquired in 2023. Under the new agreement with Nicca, Archroma will continue as the exclusive distributor of ZELAN™ DWR products and the related Teflon EcoElite™ technology to the global textile industry. Archroma will spearhead marketing initiatives for these solutions and provide technical support to mills and brands worldwide, as before. ZELAN™-finished textiles will also qualify for Archroma’s upcoming HIGH IQ® lastingrepelPRO assurance program, giving brands a well-recognized, consumer-facing mark of DWR performance, durability and sustainability. The industry’s first renewably sourced DWR, ZELAN™ R3 remains one of the most significant perfluorochemical (PFAS)-free¹ DWRs available today. It contains 63% plant-based materials², sourced from non-GMO and non-food-source feedstock, and offers excellent water repellency and outstanding durability while preserving breathability across all fibre types. “When we acquired the ZELAN™ business, we inherited more than top-tier technology—we inherited the trust that mills and brands have placed in this platform for over a decade. content: High-performance, durable functional textiles require innovative solutions that meet a wide range of consumer expectations, from lasting freshness and superior comfort to reliable protection against adverse weather conditions. SANITIZED and RUDOLF are introducing their latest innovations, demonstrating how specialized textile technologies can enhance the functional durability, comfort, and long-term wearability of modern apparel. Addressing Consumer Expectations Through Textile Innovation Consumers expect more from textiles than ever before. Functional apparel, outdoor clothing, and technical textiles must remain comfortable, functional, and reliable even after repeated wear and use. Freshness, weather protection, and long-lasting performance have become important factors influencing purchasing decisions and perceptions of product quality. In response to these growing expectations, SANITIZED and RUDOLF continue to develop technologies that address the practical challenges faced by brands, manufacturers, and end consumers. Their latest innovations are designed to enhance the long-term functionality of textiles while improving comfort, protection, and overall wearability. Long-Lasting Freshness for Functional Apparel Functional clothing is repeatedly exposed to sweat, environmental conditions, daily wear, and frequent washing. Over time, these factors can compromise the perceived comfort and performance of garments, even when the textile remains physically intact. One of the key challenges is persistent odor. Sebum and odor-causing residues can accumulate on textile fibers, resulting in unpleasant smells that may remain even after multiple washing cycles. summary: The Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) has launched three dedicated country desks for investors from China, South Korea and Japan to strengthen investor services and attract new investment to its export processing zones (EPZs) and economic zones. The desks were formally inaugurated at the ‘Meet the Investors’ event held in Dhaka on Saturday (October […] The post BEPZA launches country desks for Chinese, Korean, and Japanese investors appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: The Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) has launched three dedicated country desks for investors from China, South Korea and Japan to strengthen investor services and attract new investment to its export processing zones (EPZs) and economic zones. The desks were formally inaugurated at the ‘Meet the Investors’ event held in Dhaka on Saturday (October 10), attended by more than 100 local and foreign investors. Investors from 38 countries have invested in BEPZA’s eight EPZs and two economic zones, with China, South Korea and Japan emerging as the top three investor countries. The newly launched desks will provide direct assistance, investment-related information and guidance to existing and prospective investors from the three countries, helping streamline investment processes and strengthen communication. Speaking at the event, BEPZA Executive Chairman Major General Mohammad Moazzem Hossain said the initiative would help strengthen partnerships, address investors’ concerns and make Bangladesh’s investment environment more competitive and business-friendly. Despite global trade uncertainties and economic challenges, BEPZA signed investment agreements with 36 enterprises in the fiscal year 2025–26. Exports from its zones reached US$8.41 billion during the fiscal year, marking a 2.22 percent increase from the previous year. The executive chairman also highlighted the declaration of BEPZA Economic Zone-1, BEPZA Economic Zone-2, Jashore EPZ and Patuakhali EPZ as full-fledged zones, urging investors to expand their operations in the new zones in collaboration with supply-chain partners. title: CottonConscience combines satellite data and DNA to trace cotton
title_ko: CottonConscience는 위성 데이터와 DNA를 결합하여 목화를 추적합니다.
summary: Fashion brands could gain better evidence of cotton origins and water-related risks through a satellite-based tracking system developed by Brand Conscience. Its CottonConscience project has completed...
content: Fashion brands could gain better evidence of cotton origins and water-related risks through a satellite-based tracking system developed by Brand Conscience. Its CottonConscience project has completed a feasibility study supported by the European Space Agency (ESA), paving the way for live supply chain testing. The system combines satellite imagery, DNA tagging, farmer surveys, and digital records to trace cotton from farms to initial processing. It uses Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellite data from the European Union’s Copernicus program to identify cotton fields and assess environmental conditions. The initiative targets a key supply chain challenge: verifying sustainability claims beyond supplier declarations and paper-based audits. DNA analysis and digital records can help connect satellite-based farm information with physical cotton. Water accountability is another priority. Cotton production accounted for 8% of the global blue water footprint of crop production, according to a July 2026 analysis by Chatham House. Better farm-level data could help brands identify water risks and support more responsible sourcing. The project involves supply chain partners across Egypt, India, Türkiye, Pakistan and China. It aims to help brands verify sourcing claims and support responsible farming practices. However, the technology needs more real-world testing. It must prove that it can track products reliably, keep costs reasonable and work with existing supply chain systems before brands can use it for compliance and sustainability reporting.

title: Abhijit Chakraborty appointed Chairman & Director of IndianOil MCPI Yarn

summary: IndianOil MCPI Yarn Private Limited (IMYL), a joint venture between Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IndianOil) and MCPI Private Limited, has introduced Mr. Abhijit Chakraborty as its Chairman & Director. Mr.… The post Abhijit Chakraborty appointed Chairman & Director of IndianOil MCPI Yarn appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: IndianOil MCPI Yarn Private Limited (IMYL), a joint venture between Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IndianOil) and MCPI Private Limited, has introduced Mr. Abhijit Chakraborty as its Chairman & Director . Mr. Chakraborty currently serves as Executive Director (Projects) at IndianOil and brings extensive experience in project execution, engineering and industrial development. His appointment comes at a crucial stage in the joint venture’s development, as the partners prepare to establish a major polyester yarn manufacturing facility at Bhadrak in Odisha. The ₹5,000-crore project marks a significant step towards strengthening India’s domestic polyester manufacturing capabilities and deepening integration between the petrochemical and textile industries. The proposed facility will feature a 900-tonne-per-day continuous polymerisation unit , supported by downstream manufacturing facilities for Fully Drawn Yarn (FDY), Draw Textured Yarn (DTY) and polyester chips. Including profiles and exclusive interviews with 17 AI companies, stories and opinions from 12 different industry perspectives, and real survey feedback from around 100 voices from every level of fashion, bottled and analysed, The AI Report 2026 is essential reading for anyone interested in AI for fashion. The way fashion’s biggest campaigns are conceived, built and brought to life is continuously evolving – not just in scale, but also structure. That evolution is happening in a compressed way today: almost every global fashion brand we work with, from luxury houses like Dior and Louis Vuitton, to sportswear giants like Nike and Adidas, is rethinking its approach to promotion and presentation from the ground up, with the results then making their way as far back as product design. The result? The production workflows for fashion campaigns are also going through a moment of peak transformation, and post-production has taken on a heightened role. summary: Pakistan’s textile mills are to gain local access to precision spray finishing trials under a new initiative involving BW Converting, Archroma and Monforts. BW Converting plans to install a laboratory-scale spray-finishing unit at Archroma’s Pakistan laboratory, enabling mills to test finishing chemistries and applications on their own fabrics without initially having to carry out trials […] The post Precision spray finishing test base established in Pakistan appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Pakistan’s textile mills are to gain local access to precision spray finishing trials under a new initiative involving BW Converting, Archroma and Monforts. BW Converting plans to install a laboratory-scale spray-finishing unit at Archroma’s Pakistan laboratory, enabling mills to test finishing chemistries and applications on their own fabrics without initially having to carry out trials overseas. The three companies will outline the initiative at IGATEX Pakistan, taking place at the Expo Centre Lahore this week (October 15-18), where they will exhibit jointly through their local representative Al-Ameen Trading Corporation. The planned facility will use BW Converting’s non-contact spray application technology alongside Archroma’s textile chemistry and application expertise. Applications showing potential at laboratory level could subsequently move to larger-scale trials at the Monforts Advanced Technology Center (ATC) in Mönchengladbach, Germany. Direct route The arrangement is intended to provide a more direct route from initial formulation and application development through to testing under industrial finishing conditions. BW Converting’s Baldwin TexCoat G4 technology applies controlled quantities of finishing chemistry to one or both sides of a fabric using non-contact precision spraying. Compared with conventional processes involving higher wet pick-up, applying only the required amount of chemistry can reduce the volume of water subsequently needing to be evaporated during drying. This can lower water, chemical and energy consumption while potentially allowing higher production speeds, depending on the fabric and finishing application. Speaking on the occasion, Ambassador Lotz highlighted the importance of cultural exchange and people-to-people engagement in further deepening relations between the two countries. The official inauguration included a ribbon-cutting ceremony, an unveiling ceremony, and the traditional German toast, “Prost!” Guests also enjoyed Bavarian-themed cultural performances presented by the Goethe-Institut team, followed by a networking reception and dinner. Figure: Netherlands delegation explores green initiatives at 4A Yarn Dyeing Collet was accompanied by Wampie Libon, Ambassador for Sustainable Development, and Joris van Bommel, Ambassador of the Netherlands to Bangladesh. Representatives from Swisscontact Bangladesh, Solidaridad Network Bangladesh, Fair Wear Foundation and AWARE Bangladesh also joined the visit. The delegation toured the Savar-based facility and observed its rooftop solar plant, rainwater harvesting system, fair-price shop, childcare facility and production floor. The facility is LEED Platinum certified and was the first outerwear manufacturer to sign the UN Fashion Industry Charter for Climate Action. Afroza Shahin, Managing Director of TEAM Group, Abdullah Hil Nakib, Deputy Managing Director, and senior management officials welcomed the delegation. The visit also included a presentation on the group’s sustainability strategy and a discussion on future cooperation. Key topics included Bangladesh’s graduation from least developed country (LDC) status, the proposed Bangladesh-EU Free Trade Agreement, industrial decarbonization, traceability, digital product passports (DPPs) and upcoming EU regulations. title: Textile Innovation Expo 2026 to showcase Bangladesh’s shift towards value-driven manufacturing
summary: Bangladesh’s textile and apparel industry must move beyond its traditional reliance on low-cost labor, energy and mass production to strengthen global competitiveness through innovation, higher-va...
content: Bangladesh’s textile and apparel industry must move beyond its traditional reliance on low-cost labor, energy and mass production to strengthen global competitiveness through innovation, higher-value products and improved manufacturing efficiency, industry leaders said at a press briefing for the TIE-ITET Textile Innovation Expo 2026 . The press briefing held on 12 th October at 10:30 am at Pan Pacific Sonargaon. Figure 1: Distinguish guests of TIE-ITET Textile Innovation Expo 2026 press briefing held at Pan Pacific Sonargaon. The press briefing was attended by Engr. Md. Enayet Hossain, President of ITET Bangladesh; Eng. Imran Kader Turjo, Director of BKMEA; Md. Abdul Hamid, President of BGBA; Engr. Sumayel Mohammad Mallik, Senior Vice President of ITET; Engr. A.S.M. Hafizur Rahman Nixon, Secretary General of ITET Bangladesh and Engr. Ehsanul Karim Kaiser, Chairman of Textile Innovation Exchange (TIE) and Executive Chairman of Textile Today Innovation Hub. Enamul Hafiz Latifee, Strategic & Reporting Lead, TIE briefed the Journalist about the expo. He announced, “Textile Innovation Expo is going to be held on 12- 14 November 2026 at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB), Dhaka. It will showcase the Bangladesh Textile and Apparel sector's innovation to global buyers and brands, transforming this sector towards 'value product manufacturer' from 'cheap product manufacturer'.” Data from Eurostat cited in the briefing showed that the average EU price per kilogram of Bangladeshi apparel fell 8.47% between January and July 2026, while Vietnam’s rose 11.76%. summary: Digital Product Passport (DPP): Emerging Business and Employment Opportunities for Bangladesh’s RMG, Textile and IT Sectors A recent study involving 500 consumers in Portugal found that 79.2% had never heard of the Digital Product Passport (DPP). Although 73.4% considered environmental impact when purchasing clothing, only 35.2% were willing to pay extra for products carrying a […] The post Everyone Is Looking for a Job. Could DPP Create a New Market for Skilled Professionals and Entrepreneurs? appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Digital Product Passport (DPP): Emerging Business and Employment Opportunities for Bangladesh’s RMG, Textile and IT Sectors A recent study involving 500 consumers in Portugal found that 79.2% had never heard of the Digital Product Passport (DPP). Although 73.4% considered environmental impact when purchasing clothing, only 35.2% were willing to pay extra for products carrying a DPP. The study, conducted by researchers from the University of Minho and CITEVE, also found that awareness was significantly higher among textile and apparel professionals than among consumers outside the industry. The findings were reported by Apparel Insider. What Is a Digital Product Passport? A Digital Product Passport is a digital system designed to provide relevant product information, including material composition, product origin, manufacturing processes, durability and recycling-related information, depending on applicable requirements. As the European Union advances its sustainable product policies, DPP-related requirements could create new opportunities for businesses and professionals across the textile and apparel supply chain. New Business Opportunities for Bangladesh DPP should not be viewed solely as another compliance requirement. With proper preparation, it could create opportunities for technology-based businesses, specialised services and skilled employment. 1. DPP Software Development Bangladeshi IT companies can develop software to help garment factories manage product information, supplier records, material composition and relevant sustainability data. Subscription-based software could provide a potential recurring revenue model. 2. summary: Supply chains have long relied on documents, declarations, and trust. Rupert Hodges, Chief Strategy Officer at Oritain, explains how forensic science is replacing assumptions with physical evidence of product origin, helping businesses expose fraud, satisfy regulators, and protect their reputations. Q&A WITH RUPERT HODGES, CHIEF STRATEGY OFFICER, ORITAIN Question: Firstly, what is broken about traditional […] The post Oritain: Building Trust with Evidence appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Investing in supplier mapping, digital traceability, and better data can give companies a clearer picture of complex global supply chains than ever before. “Whilst traditional or solely digital methods can demonstrate intent and process, only verification provides a defensible source of truth in an increasingly enforcement-led environment,” says Rupert Hodges, Chief Strategy Officer, Oritain. Supply chains have long relied on documents, declarations, and trust. Rupert Hodges, Chief Strategy Officer at Oritain, explains how forensic science is replacing assumptions with physical evidence of product origin, helping businesses expose fraud, satisfy regulators, and protect their reputations. Q&A WITH RUPERT HODGES, CHIEF STRATEGY OFFICER, ORITAIN Question: Firstly, what is broken about traditional traceability? Rupert Hodges , Chief Strategy Officer (RH): Traditional traceability, or paper and digital trails of documentation and supplier declarations, are unreliable. It is easier than ever for businesses to misrepresent what they submit for their own commercial interests. Whilst traditional or solely digital methods can demonstrate intent and process, only verification provides a defensible source of truth in an increasingly enforcement-led environment. Brands that want to keep customers, regulators, and consumers onside need to upgrade to forensic verification processes where appropriate, which cannot be manipulated in the same ways. Investing in supplier mapping, digital traceability, and better data can give companies a clearer picture of complex global supply chains than ever before. Kusumgar Limited is strengthening its position… The post Kusumgar Strengthens Aerospace Focus with Long-Term Safran Partnership appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: The Indian engineered-fabrics specialist is leveraging its integrated manufacturing capabilities and expertise in high-performance materials to expand across aerospace, defence and other specialised applications. Kusumgar Limited is strengthening its position in the engineered-fabrics industry, combining specialised material expertise, integrated manufacturing and application-driven innovation to serve demanding sectors such as aerospace, defence, automotive and outdoor products. A significant milestone in this journey is the company’s recent signing of a long-term supply agreement with Safran, a global leader in the aerospace industry . The agreement reflects Safran’s commitment to working with trusted, high-quality industrial partners and creates an opportunity for Kusumgar to deepen its participation in the aerospace supply chain. The contract will support Safran’s supply chain and ongoing production programmes while contributing to Kusumgar’s expansion in the aerospace sector. Although the companies have not disclosed the specific materials and programmes covered by the agreement, the partnership marks an important step in Kusumgar’s engagement with a major international aerospace player. Engineered Fabrics at the Core Kusumgar’s core expertise lies in polyamides, polyester filaments and polyurethane chemistry, supported by specialised fabric engineering and product-development capabilities. Its portfolio addresses applications where material performance is critical, including requirements for tensile and tear strength, abrasion resistance, dimensional stability, controlled air permeability, waterproofing and durability. summary: Mr. A N M Tariqul Islam, Director (Joint Secretary), Administration and Finance, Directorate of Textile, visited the Jamalpur Textile Institute campus. During the visit, the institute’s Principal, Engineer A K M Monjurul Haque, and Instructor Engineer Kamal Hossain walked the director around the campus. They showed him the problems the institute is facing and presented […] The post Director (Joint Secretary) of the Directorate of Textile Visits Jamalpur Textile Institute Campus appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Mr. A N M Tariqul Islam, Director (Joint Secretary), Administration and Finance, Directorate of Textile, visited the Jamalpur Textile Institute campus. During the visit, the institute’s Principal, Engineer A K M Monjurul Haque, and Instructor Engineer Kamal Hossain walked the director around the campus. They showed him the problems the institute is facing and presented the situation with photographs and on-the-spot inspection. One of the main issues they pointed out was the ground sinking around several buildings. The campus soil is sandy, and because of this the earth near the buildings has been caving in. The visitors looked closely at the affected areas around the buildings. The director listened to the concerns raised by the principal and the instructor. He assured them that these problems would be solved very soon. content: DANVILLE, V.A. — October 8, 2026 — Circ® and Huafon, a leading spandex producer in China, are partnering to build and scale a new multi-phase textile-to-textile recycling site in China, expanding Circ’s global pathway to industrial scale. The project will be located within Huafon’s industrial footprint and will use Circ’s technology to process polycotton textile waste and recycle both inputs, recovering recycled PTA, recycled MEG and recycled cellulosic pulp for use in new textiles. The site will be developed in phases, with Phase 1 designed for approximately 200 metric tons of textile waste per day and additional capacity planned. The partnership brings together Circ’s polycotton recycling technology with Huafon’s manufacturing capabilities, infrastructure, and China market position. Huafon is also investing directly in the project alongside Circ and other selected investors. Huafon’s engineering, procurement, logistics, and commercial experience provide an efficient path to industrial deployment. Circ brings an established network of global brands, textile manufacturing partners, and downstream customers ready to adopt the materials the platform produces. “China is at the center of global textile production, making it a critical location for scaling textile-to-textile recycling. Huafon brings the industrial capabilities, experience, and investment to move quickly and build a platform that can scale well beyond this first site,” said Peter Majeranowski, CEO of Circ. Huafon is one of China’s leading chemical and advanced materials companies and one of the world’s largest spandex companies, with more than 30 years of experience in materials technology, innovation, and chemical manufacturing. content: The two-day "Textile Fest Bangladesh 1.0" was held for the first time at the National Institute of Textile Engineering and Research (NITER) in Savar. Organized by the NITER Textile Club on October 8 and 9, the festival brought students from across the country, industry representatives and corporate leaders together on one platform. Competitions, discussions with industry figures, career seminars, a job fair, a fashion show and cultural performances kept the campus lively for two days. The program began on Thursday (October 8) with registration at 8:30 am. From 9 am, competitions got under way, including Tex Olympiad, mock interview, case competition and innovative speech, while stalls from various organizations were set up. More than 3,000 students and over 150 industry and corporate representatives took part on the first day. Dhaka-19 MP Dr Dewan Mohammad Salahuddin Babu was the chief guest, and Bangladesh Textile Mills Corporation (BTMC) Chairman Brig Gen S M Zahid Hasan was the special guest. Speakers included Md Safayat Hossain, General Manager of Epyllion Group, who presented the "7E" formula; Kazi Feroz Hossain; Prof Dr Md Shah-e-Alam, Vice-Chancellor of Shanto-Mariam University of Creative Technology; BTMC Director (Finance and Audit) Noore Khaja Alamin; and NITER Director Prof Dr Ashequl Alam Rana. Banna, convener of the NITER Textile Club, pledged to continue the club's activities to increase student engagement. Guests visited the stalls around noon while judging continued. After the lunch break came dance and music performances and a competitive fashion show. The first day ended at around 9:30 pm. title: Bangladesh’s power expansion faces the test of fuel, finance, and reliability
summary: Key insights: Bangladesh plans 12,940MW of new capacity by 2030, including 10,000 MW of solar and 2,940 MW of coal. Electricity demand reached 18,178MW, while projected September generation was 15,85...
content: Key insights: Bangladesh plans 12,940MW of new capacity by 2030, including 10,000 MW of solar and 2,940 MW of coal. Electricity demand reached 18,178MW, while projected September generation was 15,859MW. Solar capacity must rise from about 1,452MW to 10,000MW, requiring about 8,550MW of new capacity in four years. Bangladesh is planning a major expansion of its power system, but the immediate challenge is closing the gap between electricity demand and usable generation. Figure: Looking ahead, the medium-term roadmap targets 12,940 MW between 2028 and 2030 to meet projected peak demand of 20,000–25,000 MW The country reached 29,143 megawatts (MW) of grid-connected installed capacity by August 2026. However, peak electricity demand hit 18,178 MW on September 14, up 17% from 15,570 MW a year earlier. September generation was projected at only 15,859 MW, leaving a 2,319 MW shortfall. Natural gas remains the largest generation source, accounting for 43–44% of installed capacity with over 12,000 MW. Yet daily gas supply averaged only 2,610 million cubic feet (mmcfd) against an approved demand of 3,800 mmcfd. This supply shortage capped gas-based generation at 5,977 MW in September. Weak coal availability further forced the grid to rely on costlier liquid fuels, pushing projected liquid-fuel generation to 3,791 MW. Under the government's 2026–27 supply plan, the grid allocates 6,000 MW each from gas and coal, 4,000 MW from liquid fuels, 2,500 MW from regional imports, and up to 4,000 MW from rooftop solar. title: Lycra advances plant-based spandex with 70% renewable content
title_ko: Lycra, 70% 재생 가능 콘텐츠로 식물성 spandex 발전
summary: The Lycra Company is advancing plant-based spandex with 70% renewable content from US-grown field corn. The fiber can reduce its carbon footprint by up to 45% while maintaining the stretch and recover...
content: The Lycra Company is advancing plant-based spandex with 70% renewable content from US-grown field corn. The fiber can reduce its carbon footprint by up to 45% while maintaining the stretch and recovery performance of conventional Lycra fiber, according to a third-party-reviewed life cycle assessment. Figure: Global fiber production reached an estimated 139 million tons in 2025, while textile-to-textile recycling accounted for only 0.76% of total fiber production. The fiber has entered commercial applications, including swimwear by Italian brand Arena and denim by Danish brand Only & Sons. Lycra also showcased a plant-based denim collection during Climate Week in New York in September 2026, combining its renewable fiber with lower-footprint cotton. The development comes as textile manufacturers face growing pressure to reduce material-related emissions. Global fiber production reached an estimated 139 million tons in 2025, while textile-to-textile recycling accounted for only 0.76% of total fiber production, according to Textile Exchange’s Materials Market Report 2026 . Alongside renewable feedstocks, Lycra is developing pilot-stage technology to recover spandex from textile waste blended with nylon and polyester. Commercial-scale recycling remains a challenge because these fibers are difficult to separate efficiently. For apparel manufacturers, renewable spandex offers a potential route to lower the carbon footprint of stretch fabrics without compromising performance. However, wider adoption will depend on cost, supply availability and credible environmental data. Scaling fiber recovery from blended textiles will also be critical to advancing circular production beyond the use of renewable raw materials.

summary: The Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) has launched dedicated country desks for investors from China, South Korea and Japan to strengthen investor support and attract new investment...
content: The Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) has launched dedicated country desks for investors from China, South Korea and Japan to strengthen investor support and attract new investment to its export processing zones (EPZs) and economic zones. The three desks were inaugurated at a “Meet the Investors” event in Dhaka on October 10. The initiative targets BEPZA’s three leading investor countries and aims to improve communication, provide tailored guidance, and simplify investment-related services. Investors from 38 countries have invested in BEPZA’s eight EPZs and two economic zones, according to a press release. The authority expects the new desks to help existing investors expand their operations while encouraging new investors to enter Bangladesh. During FY2025-26, BEPZA signed investment agreements with 36 enterprises. Exports from its zones reached $8.41 billion, up 2.22% from the previous fiscal year. New zones offer expansion opportunities BEPZA has declared BEPZA Economic Zone-1, BEPZA Economic Zone-2, Jashore EPZ and Patuakhali EPZ as full-fledged zones. The authority has invited investors to explore opportunities in these locations and expand operations with their supply chain partners. However, infrastructure development and simpler policies remain important to attracting more foreign investment. Million Park, General secretary of the Korea-Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industry, highlighted the potential for stronger business ties between Bangladesh and South Korea. He called for infrastructure improvements and policy simplification to attract more Korean investors. summary: The Nature Conservancy (TNC) has launched the Microfiber Action Alliance (MAA), bringing together major apparel and outdoor brands to reduce microfiber pollution across the textile value chain. Nike,...
content: The Nature Conservancy (TNC) has launched the Microfiber Action Alliance (MAA), bringing together major apparel and outdoor brands to reduce microfiber pollution across the textile value chain. Nike, Patagonia, Under Armour, lululemon, Cotopaxi and REI Co-op are among its founding participants. Announced on October 6, 2026, the initiative aims to accelerate the adoption of science-based solutions, test practical interventions, and share findings across the industry. It will work with participating companies to identify where microfiber pollution occurs and determine which measures can deliver meaningful reductions at scale. Microfiber pollution extends beyond synthetic textiles. Fibers can be released from polyester, nylon, and acrylic, as well as natural materials such as cotton and wool. Dyeing, softeners, and other textile treatments can also affect the environmental behavior of released fibers. Pollution can occur during textile manufacturing, garment use, washing, and disposal. Research published in PLOS ONE found substantial differences in microfiber shedding among textile samples. In tests covering 37 materials, fiber loss ranged from 9.6 milligrams to 1,240 milligrams per kilogram of textile per wash. The findings highlight the role of fabric construction, material selection, and finishing in reducing fiber release. These results are specific to the tested samples and do not represent all textiles. The alliance builds on existing industry research and collaboration, including work by The Microfibre Consortium, which develops scientific tools and methods to measure fiber fragmentation and support reductions across textile supply chains. content: The Federation of Bangladesh Human Resource Organizations (FBHRO) successfully held the Corporate Council Members’ Registration Launching Program this evening at Sheraton Hotel, Dhaka, bringing together a distinguished gathering of senior HR professionals from diverse industries. The program gave newly registered Corporate Council Members an opportunity to introduce themselves, exchange professional experiences, and receive their membership certificates. Addressing the gathering, Mr. Musharrof Hossain, President of FBHRO, highlighted the significance of Corporate Council Membership, describing it as a mark of senior professional standing within the HR community and an opportunity to contribute more meaningfully to advancing the HR profession. Mr. Farid A. Sobhani, Vice President of FBHRO and President of the Bangladesh Society for Human Capital Management (BSHCM), welcomed all members and urged them to uphold the highest ethical standards in HR practices. He also invited the participants to join BSHCM, a newly registered HR professional association, to strengthen professional collaboration, promote ethical HR practices, and contribute to the development of human capital management in Bangladesh. Professor Moinuddin Chowdhury, Secretary General of FBHRO, skillfully conducted the program, facilitated the proceedings, and encouraged active engagement among participants. The gathering reflected a shared commitment to building a stronger, more connected, and professionally responsible HR community in Bangladesh. The event also served as an opportunity to invite Corporate Council Members to participate in the 8th National HR Convention 2026, scheduled for 28 November 2026 at Sheraton Hotel, Dhaka. summary: KANSAS CITY, Mo. — October 8, 2026 — eVent® Fabrics, a supplier of breathable waterproof, weatherproof, and windproof laminate technologies, is proud to announce its partnership with Rocky Mountain ATV, which has selected eVent’s high-performance alpineST 3-layer fabric for its new 2027 MSR Xplorer ADV Jacket and MSR Xplorer ADV Pants. content: KANSAS CITY, Mo. — October 8, 2026 — eVent® Fabrics, a supplier of breathable waterproof, weatherproof, and windproof laminate technologies, is proud to announce its partnership with Rocky Mountain ATV, which has selected eVent’s high-performance alpineST 3-layer fabric for its new 2027 MSR Xplorer ADV Jacket and MSR Xplorer ADV Pants. Adventure riding can put riders through a wide range of conditions in a single day, from heat and high exertion to rain, wind, and changing temperatures. The new MSR Xplorer ADV system is designed around those demands, combining waterproof, breathable protection with durable construction, integrated armor, and extensive ventilation. “Adventure riding can subject apparel to some pretty unique demands,” said Chad Kelly, Vice President of eVent Fabrics. “You can go from a hot, exposed stretch of trail to rain, altitude, and colder conditions in the same ride. The MSR Xplorer ADV is designed around that reality, and alpineST gives a waterproof, breathable foundation that helps riders stay comfortable as conditions change.” The MSR Xplorer ADV Jacket features an eVent alpineST 3-layer main body fabric with a C0 DWR finish for waterproof and breathable protection. SuperFabric overlays at the shoulders and elbows provide additional abrasion resistance, while removable D3O Level 1 shoulder, elbow, and back protectors adds impact protection. Four large zippered intake vents at the biceps and chest, two double-headed wrist and forearm vents, and two large rear exhaust vents allow riders to actively manage airflow as temperatures rise. The MSR Xplorer ADV Pants use the same eVent alpineST 3-layer fabric and C0 DWR finish, with SuperFabric overlays at the knees and 500D Cordura® in high-wear areas. title: How technology upgradation can help Bangladesh’s textile sector regain competitiveness
title_ko: 기술 업그레이드가 Bangladesh의 섬유 부문이 경쟁력을 회복하는 데 어떻게 도움이 될 수 있습니까?
summary: Bangladesh’s textile industry has built much of its strength on a solid backward linkage base, with spinning playing a particularly important role in supporting the country’s ready made garment secto...
content: Bangladesh’s textile industry has built much of its strength on a solid backward linkage base, with spinning playing a particularly important role in supporting the country’s ready made garment sector. For decades, investment in spinning capacity helped reduce dependence on imported yarn, shorten sourcing lead times and strengthen the domestic textile value chain. Today, however, the economics of spinning have become much more difficult. Gas and electricity costs have risen sharply. Wages are higher, financing remains expensive, imported raw materials are costly, and competition from regional suppliers continues to put pressure on yarn prices. At the same time, many mills are still operating with machinery and production systems installed more than a decade ago. Under these conditions, technology upgradation is no longer simply about producing more. It is increasingly about producing at a cost that allows a mill to remain competitive. The challenge becomes even more serious when working capital is considered. In Bangladesh, textile mills often operate with much longer working capital cycles than competitors in countries such as India and China. When capital remains tied up for several months, financing costs rise and operating flexibility declines. This means that mills cannot depend only on volume growth. The next phase of competitiveness will have to come from better energy efficiency, higher machine productivity, lower waste, more automation and a broader product mix. Energy efficiency must come first Energy is now one of the most important factors affecting spinning cost. Older machinery generally consumes significantly more power than modern systems. Where the design and selection phase of a new polymer typically takes years, polySCOUT brings it down to weeks. The technology has been […]
content: AMSTERDAM — October 9, 2026 — TNO today launches polySCOUT, an independent Dutch AI company that designs polymers to specification. Target properties and regulatory constraints go in; lab-validated candidate materials come out. Where the design and selection phase of a new polymer typically takes years, polySCOUT brings it down to weeks. The technology has been developed within TNO since 2022, and TNO becomes a shareholder in the new company. To mark the launch, the founders ring the gong at Euronext Amsterdam this morning. Why now Plastics are everywhere: 431 million tonnes were produced worldwide in 2024 (PlasticsEurope). Yet the molecules the industry relies on are largely a century old, and regulation is now changing faster than the chemistry. Since 20 July 2026, bisphenol A has been banned in food contact materials in the EU. The European microplastics restriction phases out synthetic polymer microparticles category by category through 2035. A broad PFAS restriction is in preparation. Every deadline means the same thing: a material has to go, and its replacement has to perform at least as well.”Forced substitution is a performance problem with a deadline,” says Michaël van der Jagt, co-founder and CEO of polySCOUT. “Conventional polymer development succeeds in five to ten percent of cases. Not because chemists lack skill, but because the search space is unimaginably large: more than 1060 possible polymer structures. We don’t make R&D faster. We make it start in the right place.” How it works polySCOUT turns the classical development process around. title: Denmark sets Three-Year roadmap for EU-ready textile sector
summary: Denmark has launched a national textile action plan to reduce textile production and consumption while preparing businesses for upcoming European Union (EU) requirements. Figure: Denmark sets a three...
content: Denmark has launched a national textile action plan to reduce textile production and consumption while preparing businesses for upcoming European Union (EU) requirements. Figure: Denmark sets a three-year roadmap for EU-ready textile sector.Courtesy: Collected The three-year program will run from 2026 to 2029. It includes nine initiatives and has a budget of DKK 40 million (approximately $6 million). The plan focuses on three areas: business readiness, circular infrastructure and skills development. These priorities aim to help the textile sector adapt to changing regulatory requirements and support a more circular textile system. The action plan seeks to prepare textile businesses for upcoming EU requirements. As sustainability and circularity become increasingly important in European textile policy, businesses will need to adapt their operations and practices. The focus on circular infrastructure also highlights the importance of developing systems that support more efficient textile use and resource recovery. Such infrastructure can help create the conditions needed to reduce textile waste and improve material circulation. The Danish plan is a national action framework rather than new legislation. It does not establish binding national targets for textile production, consumption or waste reduction. Instead, it sets out initiatives to guide the sector's transition between 2026 and 2029. Denmark's strategy reflects a broader shift in European textile policy toward addressing both production and consumption. For textile manufacturers and exporters serving the European market, the direction of such national initiatives is worth monitoring. title: Recover™ introduces color-matched recycled cotton and polyester blend

summary: Spanish textile recycling company Recover™ has launched RecoverOne, a recycled cotton and polyester fiber blend designed to eliminate downstream overdyeing and simplify textile production. The compan...
content: Spanish textile recycling company Recover™ has launched RecoverOne, a recycled cotton and polyester fiber blend designed to eliminate downstream overdyeing and simplify textile production. The company said the ready-to-spin blend combines mechanically recycled cotton with recycled polyester in color-matched ratios tailored to different textile applications. By matching the fiber colors during blending, RecoverOne is designed to remove the need for additional dyeing after fabric production. The launch highlights an approach to integrating color selection into recycled fiber development, potentially helping textile manufacturers simplify processing and reduce reliance on downstream overdyeing. For textile manufacturers, the blend offers an option to incorporate recycled fibers while addressing production requirements related to color consistency and processing efficiency. Its application-specific formulation also allows the blend to be adapted to different textile uses. Recover™, based in Spain, develops recycled textile materials, with mechanical cotton recycling forming part of its product portfolio.

Announced as the industry marked World Circular Textiles Day on October 8, the latest customers are Akij Textile Mills in Bangladesh, Material Return in the United States and Artistic Denim […] The post Trützschler Expands TRUECYCLED Network With Three New Customers appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Trützschler Group has expanded the international customer network for its TRUECYCLED textile recycling technology, adding new reference installations in Bangladesh, Pakistan and the United States. Announced as the industry marked World Circular Textiles Day on October 8, the latest customers are Akij Textile Mills in Bangladesh, Material Return in the United States and Artistic Denim Mills in Pakistan. The additions reflect growing interest in technologies capable of transforming pre-consumer and post-consumer textile waste into secondary fibres suitable for producing new yarns. TRUECYCLED Connects Recycling With Spinning Preparation TRUECYCLED is Trützschler’s integrated solution for the mechanical recycling and spinning preparation of textile waste. The process can cover cutting and tearing textile waste, opening, cleaning and blending the recovered fibres, carding and drawing the resulting material before it enters the spinning process. One of the main technical challenges in mechanical textile recycling is the loss of fibre length. Cutting and tearing fabrics create fibres that are generally shorter and more variable than virgin raw materials. Unopened yarn and fabric particles can also remain in the material stream. If these secondary fibres undergo overly aggressive processing, additional fibre damage can reduce usable yield and make it more difficult to produce stable, homogeneous yarn. Trützschler addresses this challenge by coordinating the tearing and spinning-preparation stages. Machine settings and process configurations are selected to limit unnecessary fibre shortening while ensuring that the recovered material is sufficiently opened, cleaned and blended. content: Fabrica Knit Composite Ltd. (FKCL), a concern of Fashion Power Group, has signed a two-year consultancy agreement with Panacea Private Consulting Group to strengthen operational performance, productivity, and manufacturing excellence. The agreement was signed on 9 October 2026 at the Fashion Power Group head office in Dhaka under the initiative titled “FKCL EXCEL 360.” Mr. Mijanur Rahman, Managing Director of Fashion Power Group and Vice President of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), signed the agreement on behalf of Fashion Power Group, while Dr. Azim Mohammad, Managing Director of Panacea Private Consulting Group, signed on behalf of Panacea. Directors, Assistant Vice Presidents (AVPs), and other senior representatives from both organizations attended the signing ceremony, marking the beginning of a two-year collaboration focused on sustainable operational improvement. The engagement will focus on strengthening industrial engineering (IE), improving productivity, enhancing production planning and control, optimizing capacity utilization, and establishing more effective, data-driven performance management systems. The initiative will also emphasize systematic problem-solving, operational discipline, and continuous improvement across relevant manufacturing functions. Panacea Private Consulting Group provides consulting services in lean manufacturing, industrial engineering, and manufacturing excellence. Through this engagement, the organizations aim to strengthen operational systems and develop sustainable improvement practices aligned with the factory’s business objectives. content: US textile recycling technology developer Circ is joining forces with Chinese chemicals and fibre manufacturing giant Huafon to establish a large-scale textile-to-textile recycling operation in China, with an initial processing capacity of approximately 200 tons of textile waste per day. The project will be developed within Huafon’s existing industrial infrastructure, combining Circ’s technology for recovering both polyester and cellulose from blended fabrics with the Chinese group’s manufacturing capabilities, engineering resources and established supply chains. Significantly, Huafon will also invest directly in the venture alongside Circ and other selected investors, providing both industrial expertise and financial backing for its development. The new facility will be built in phases, with the first designed to process approximately 200 tons of textile waste daily, equivalent to around 73,000 tons annually if operated continuously at full capacity. Further expansion is planned. The partnership represents another major step in Circ’s efforts to commercialise its recycling technology, alongside the company’s first industrial-scale facility currently under development in France. © Huafon Industrial backing Headquartered in Wenzhou, Zhejiang Province, Huafon is one of China’s largest chemical and advanced materials manufacturers and a major global producer of spandex and polyurethane materials. Founded in 1991, the group employs more than 20,000 people worldwide and operates across polyurethane, polyamide, bio-based materials and other industrial sectors. title: The ASOS Hack Is Another Reminder Of Fashion’s Fast-Growing Cyber-Risk Surface
summary: A serious story and a slightly funnier one have drawn renewed attention to spectrum of data that fashion captures, aggregates, and deploys in service of personalisation. That data is fast becoming an acute risk thanks to the patchwork of third party systems that hold it, and a brace of governance challenges around it. The post The ASOS Hack Is Another Reminder Of Fashion’s Fast-Growing Cyber-Risk Surface appeared first on The Interline .
content: Key Takeaways Earlier this week, UK shoppers who had the ASOS app installed received a notification through it, from a hacking group that claimed to have compromised the brand’s third party data cloud. Yesterday, the scope of the breach was revealed to contain more than the personal contact details originally disclosed, including individual search histories and personalisation levers. As with the recent spate of retail-focused cybersecurity incidents, the group claiming responsibility obtained access to ASOS’ data through external systems and social engineering rather than direct intrusion into first party software. And while AI is involved in the brand’s personalisation pipeline, this does not seem to have been an AI-aided attack. Brands have continued to turn to personalisation platforms and strategies to enhance their customer engagement, creating new utility for personal data that then, in turn, creates a greater incentive to capture and retain that data – extending the industry’s risk surface over time. Hacks like the one ASOS is facing, and viral stories like Amazon’s more benign profile-building, bring that risk back into the consumer consciousness. The Interline doesn’t like to generalise, but if you’re a frequent purchaser of fast fashion, you’re probably accustomed to getting a notification or two from the biggest names in that segment. No ASOS shopper, though, expected the ping they received this Tuesday, which came from the brand’s official iOS app, but which was signed off by a previously-unknown hacking group calling itself Xuanyewen. content: Brussels, 9 October 2026 – EURATEX has joined 43 other European industry organisations in calling for stronger EU trade defence measures to protect European manufacturing, safeguard jobs and ensure fair competition in the Single Market. In a joint statement, the 44 organisations urge EU Member States and the European Commission to take decisive action against unfair trade practices, persistent global overcapacity and market distortions driven by state subsidies. The initiative brings together industries from across the European manufacturing value chain, including textiles, chemicals, metals, automotive suppliers and other strategic sectors. European industry faces growing pressure European manufacturers are operating in an increasingly challenging global environment. High energy costs, growing international competition and unfair trade practices are putting additional pressure on industrial competitiveness. The situation is particularly concerning as state-driven overcapacity and underpriced imports continue to distort global markets. According to Eurostat figures cited in the statement, the EU’s trade deficit in goods with China reached approximately €359.8 billion in 2025 , equivalent to almost €1 billion per day. For EURATEX, ensuring fair competition is essential to maintaining a strong European textile and clothing industry, supporting quality employment and encouraging investment in European production. content: AMSTERDAM — October 6, 2026 — Fashion for Good today announces the launch of the Cotton Reloop Matrix Project, a cross-industry initiative that will map and physically validate the quality of commercially available recycled cotton yarns against brand specifications, giving the industry a data-backed overview of how quality, price, and recycled content intersect. The project is convened with Fashion for Good partners Arvind, BESTSELLER, C&A, Interloop, Reformation, Shahi, and ecosystem partner Uster. Cotton accounts for 19% of global fibre production and a core part of the material mix. Although alternative recycling pathways exist to utilise cotton-rich textile waste feedstock, they do not make a cotton output. Therefore, mechanical recycling is a crucial pathway to utilise waste and create recycled cotton yarns and fabrics. Through the mechanical recycling process, textile waste is shredded and re-opened into loose fibres that can be respun into yarn. However, shredding shortens and weakens the fibres, so only 45 to 50% of the input survives as usable material. The rest is lost as short fibres and processing waste, and because the surviving fibres are shorter than virgin cotton, spinners can only blend a limited share back into new yarn. In practice, that caps most yarns at around 10% recycled content: any higher and the fabric isn’t durable enough for commercial use. While recyclers have available capacities, integrating a meaningful percentage of recycled cotton remains complex for brands navigating trade-offs around quality and price. Testing happens in isolation, with recyclers and brands working from separate data sets, and no shared reference comparison to close the gap between them. title: Building a stronger domestic textile value chain
title_ko: 더욱 강력한 국내 섬유 Value Chain 구축
summary: The government's decision to raise the cash incentive from 1.5 percent to 5 percent for the use of domestically produced yarn and fabric in Bangladesh's Ready-Made Garment (RMG) industry is timely. Am...
content: The government's decision to raise the cash incentive from 1.5 percent to 5 percent for the use of domestically produced yarn and fabric in Bangladesh's Ready-Made Garment (RMG) industry is timely. Amidst intense global competition in the apparel sector, rising production costs, and various challenges facing the country's spinning and textile industries, this move could strengthen the local textile sector. An increase in demand for locally produced yarn and fabric could yield benefits for spinning, dyeing, knitting, and other allied industries. Furthermore, it could create new market opportunities for spinning mills that are currently operating below full capacity or facing financial difficulties. However, this decision should not be viewed merely as an increase in export incentives. Its significance is far-reaching, as it is directly linked to Bangladesh's long-term industrial capacity, local value addition, reduction of import dependency, and foreign currency savings. Consequently, a significant portion of the entire value chain—from yarn to fabric and fabric to the final garment—can be completed within Bangladesh. Increased use of local inputs can help reduce import reliance, save foreign currency, generate demand for related industries, and boost local value addition. This is where the 5 percent incentive holds significant potential. Additionally, the government's decision to withdraw the zero-duty import facility for 10–30 count cotton yarn under the bonded warehouse system should also be viewed in this context. content: Asahi Kasei will bring together nine textile manufacturers at Performance Days in Munich next week, illustrating the increasingly varied ways in which stretch is being engineered into performance and lifestyle fabrics. Seven European manufacturers – Borgini Jersey, Brugnoli, Cifra, Penn Solutions, Reda, Sitip and Tiba Tricot – will be joined by Japanese warp knitting specialists Imai Kigyojo and Kawada Knitting Group at the Roica stand at the October 13-14 event. Rather than presenting a single collection, the partners will demonstrate applications ranging from highly breathable and three-dimensional sportswear structures to seamless garments, fine Merino wool fabrics and lightweight Japanese tricot. A recurring material within several of the developments is Roica V550, Asahi Kasei’s stretch fibre designed to partially degrade under specified conditions. Borgini Jersey has incorporated V550 into knitted fabrics including breathable meshes intended to accelerate drying and manage body climate, as well as three-dimensional structures designed to reduce fabric cling during exercise. Italian circular knitter Brugnoli, meanwhile, will show Explosive Amni V550, combining Amni Soul Eco polyamide with Roica V550. The fabric forms part of the company’s Explosive Technology platform, which is designed to provide elasticity and body support while retaining freedom of movement. Cifra provides a different interpretation through its Warp Knit Seamless (WKS) technology. The process enables garments and components incorporating detailed motifs to be produced with reduced material waste, and has been employed in Cifra’s continuing work with Austrian bodywear specialist Wolford. content: SINGAPORE — October 5, 2026 — BrilliA Incorporated, a one-stop service and solution provider for ladies’ intimate apparel brands worldwide, today announced that it has acquired a majority equity interest in Neubodi Holdings Sdn. Bhd. (“Neubodi”), an established Malaysian lingerie brand and specialty retailer, effective August 1, 2026. The acquisition marks BrilliA’s strategic expansion into branded specialty retail in Southeast Asia and broadens the Company’s business beyond its existing B2B supply and design operations. Founded in 2008, Neubodi is known for its proprietary holistic bra fitting approach and broad size range of 72 bra sizes, spanning cup sizes A to I and band sizes 65 to 100. The company operates 11 retail stores across the Klang Valley, Penang and Johor, including locations in major retail destinations such as Mid Valley Megamall, 1 Utama, Sunway Pyramid, and IOI City Mall, alongside e-commerce and social media channels. Through its combination of specialist fitting expertise, physical retail locations and digital consumer engagement, Neubodi provides BrilliA with an established platform for serving end consumers directly and developing its branded retail capabilities. Tan See See, co-founder of Neubodi with more than 15 years of experience in the intimate apparel industry, will continue to serve as Chief Executive Officer of Neubodi. Ooi Kit Joyce will also continue as part of the senior management team. content: TOKYO — September 28, 2026 — Teijin Limited today announced new grades of SOLFIGA®, its family of polyphenylene sulfide (PPS) compounds, which offer excellent sliding properties without intentionally added per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). The new grades are also designed to help customers balance wear and friction performances with regulatory compliance. SOLFIGA® PPS compound pellets Teijin already supplies polybutylene naphthalate (PBN) resin with good sliding properties as its PFAS-Free product. By expanding PFAS-Free high-performance resin lineup, Teijin will further enhance its ability to meet increasingly diverse customer needs. As with existing SOLFIGA® lineup, the PFAS-Free SOLFIGA® grades incorporate carbon fiber and aramid fiber as reinforcement. The carbon fiber-reinforced SOLFIGA® sliding grade provides high strength and rigidity for components used under high-load conditions. Gears using SOLFIGA® PPS compound (prototype) The aramid fiber-reinforced SOLFIGA® sliding grade reduces coefficient of friction (CoF)—one indicator of sliding performance—by approximately 70 percent compared with conventional products that do not use sliding agents. Its flexibility can help reduce damage to mating materials while allowing easier adjustment during assembly. Both types of SOLFIGA® sliding compounds offer high wear resistance for longer service life. Like Teijin’s PBN resin, they are less likely to scratch metal components such as aluminum. Also, Teijin can formulate them to produce sliding parts for a wide range of conditions by varying the amount of high-performance fibers. content: The National Institute of Textile Engineering and Research (NITER) in Savar held the Fresher’s Reception 2026 for its 16th batch on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, at the central field of the campus. Organized by NITER administration, the event had Shafiqul Islam Sarker, Vice President of the Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA), as chief guest. Nur-E-Khaja Alamin, a director of the association, attended as special guest. NITER Director Dr. Md. Ashequl Alam Rana presided over the program. The day began at 10:00 AM with recitations from the Quran and the Gita, followed by the national anthem. The guests then offered motivational words and career guidance to the newcomers. A major highlight was the set of stalls run by NITER’s clubs and societies, which drew crowds of curious freshers. Participating organizations included the NITER Journalists’ Association, Debating Society, Computer Club, Cultural Club, Career Club, and Film and Photographic Society. The second half of the program was a cultural evening centered on performances by the new students. Songs, dance, recitation, drama, and a ramp show filled the venue with a festive atmosphere. content: Thermore’s EVOdown recycled insulation is being used across five men’s and women’s styles in the new Patagonia Heyes Peak collection. Designed for everyday wear in changing and transitional weather, the Heyes Peak range includes a jacket, parka, hoody and three-in-one parka. The garments combine layer-friendly linings with EVOdown insulation to provide warmth and softness without excessive bulk. The Heyes Peak Jacket uses 80 gsm EVOdown with a shell made from NetPlus 100% post-consumer recycled nylon ripstop. NetPlus material is produced from recycled fishing nets, while the shell also has a durable water-repellent treatment made without intentionally added PFAS. Thermore EVOdown is made with fibres 100% recycled from PET bottles and has been developed to combine the soft handle and loft associated with down with the durability and easy care of synthetic insulation. The insulation is certified to Oeko-Tex Standard 100, the Global Recycled Standard (GRS) and bluesign requirements. Styles across the Heyes Peak collection are also manufactured in Fair Trade Certified factories. “We’re thrilled to partner with Patagonia on the Heyes Peak collection,” said Laura Beachy, senior vice president of global marketing and communications at Thermore. “Thermore EVOdown gives Patagonia a fill that meets its sustainability standards across five styles without asking it to compromise on warmth or comfort.” The Heyes Peak Jacket uses a 1.2 oz, 20-denier NetPlus ripstop shell alongside the recycled insulation, extending Patagonia’s use of recycled materials through different components of the garment. “The best materials are the ones that help us meet our customers’ needs while reducing our impact,” said Mark Little, senior business unit director at Patagonia Lifestyle Essentials + Graphi

content: The Lycra Company will highlight progress in producing spandex from renewable raw materials and developing textile-to-textile recycling technology at the Textile Exchange Conference 2026, taking place in Vancouver, Canada, from October 12-16. The company has now reached commercial-scale production of its Renewable Lycra fibre, which contains 70% plant-based material, while continuing to develop processes for recovering and recycling spandex from waste textiles. The renewable fibre uses dent corn grown primarily in Iowa, USA, as a feedstock to replace a significant proportion of the petroleum-derived raw materials traditionally used in spandex production. According to a comparative life cycle assessment conducted by Ramboll this year, the bio-based fibre can reduce its carbon footprint by up to 45% compared to conventional Lycra fibre, while maintaining equivalent stretch and recovery properties. The assessment specifically compares fibres made with bio-derived and fossil-derived polytetramethylene ether glycol (PTMEG), a key component in spandex production. Alongside this commercial development, Lycra is working with textile recycling specialists to address one of the more difficult challenges facing the industry – the recovery of elastane from blended fabrics. Spandex is widely used in combination with polyester, nylon and other fibres to provide stretch and shape retention, but its presence complicates conventional textile recycling processes. Over the past few years, Lycra has collaborated with recycling companies worldwide to develop methods of separating spandex from other fibres in pre-consumer textile waste and processing the recovered material into new spandex fibres. title: From mass production to precision cutting at Edwin Base

summary: Japanese denim manufacturer Akita Hose has transformed a former mass-production jeans factory into a specialist operation producing smaller batches of high-value garments, supported by automated cutting technology from Shima Seiki. Established in 1973, Akita Hose is part of the Edwin Group’s Japanese manufacturing operations and previously employed around 100 people producing approximately 3,000 pairs of […] The post From mass production to precision cutting at Edwin Base appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Japanese denim manufacturer Akita Hose has transformed a former mass-production jeans factory into a specialist operation producing smaller batches of high-value garments, supported by automated cutting technology from Shima Seiki. Established in 1973, Akita Hose is part of the Edwin Group’s Japanese manufacturing operations and previously employed around 100 people producing approximately 3,000 pairs of jeans a day. Today, its workforce has been reduced to around 30, while production has shifted almost entirely from jeans to more complex garments such as denim jackets. The factory now handles orders as small as 50-100 garments for brands including Edwin, Lee, Wrangler and Something, as well as jackets destined for overseas markets. The transformation culminated in October 2024, when equipment previously distributed across three buildings was consolidated into a single facility and the operation was relaunched as Edwin Base. P-CAM R Central to the reorganisation was the replacement of two ageing industrial cutting machines with a single, more compact Shima Seiki P-CAM R automated cutting system. The previous machines dated from the factory’s high-volume production era and occupied considerable floor space. Their age was also creating concerns about maintenance, safety and the availability of technical support. Akita Hose needed a replacement capable of handling denim accurately at relatively high speeds, while accommodating frequent changes in styles and production quantities. Compatibility with its existing CAD data was another important consideration. content: The country’s largest textile festival, ‘Textile Fest Bangladesh 1.0’, has been held for the first time at the campus of the National Institute of Textile Engineering and Research (NITER) in Savar. Organized by the NITER Textile Club, the event aimed to bring textile and apparel students, industry representatives, and corporate leaders together on one platform. On the first day of the two-day event, more than 3,000 students from universities and institutions across the country and over 150 industry and corporate representatives took part. The festival focused on the sector’s potential, innovation, careers, and industry-academia linkage. Dewan Mohammad Salahuddin, Member of Parliament for Dhaka-19, attended as chief guest. Special guests included Brigadier General S M Zahid Hasan, Chairman of the Bangladesh Textile Mills Corporation (BTMC), among others. A key attraction was the series of career seminars and talk shows, where experienced professionals discussed the industry’s current state, opportunities, and career paths with students. A job fair and career networking sessions gave participants direct access to company representatives. To showcase young people’s creativity and skills, the festival featured a textile and apparel exhibition and a fashion show. Competitions included TexOlympiad, TexTech Hackathon, a 180-Second Innovative Pitch, Mock Interview, and Photography, with a total prize pool of BDT 2.5 lakh. The festival closes with a mega live concert and stand-up comedy, along with a raffle draw for visitors. As the first event of the NITER Textile Club, the festival has generated strong interest among students and textile stakeholders. content: The textile industry is entering a groundbreaking era. Manufacturers face rising energy prices, growing sustainability demands, increasing labor shortages, and an unprecedented need for flexibility. For a globally active textile industry, where competitiveness is closely linked to production efficiency and cost leadership, this means that technology is no longer merely a means of improving operational processes – it is increasingly becoming a strategic differentiator. Against this backdrop, Barmag will present a innovation portfolio at India ITME that goes far beyond incremental machine upgrades. In doing so, the company is laying the foundation for what it calls “A New Era” of textile production. At the center of this transformation stands one development in particular: Barmag POY 2.0. André Wissenberg, Head of Marketing, Corporate Communications and Public Affairs at Barmag Every few years, an innovation emerges that fundamentally changes how an industry thinks about production. Barmag believes POY 2.0 represents exactly such a moment. The new spinning concept is the result of a complete re-evaluation of the entire POY process chain, from spinning and quenching to winding, parallel with a digital process control. Rather than improving isolated components, engineers reimagined the interaction between all process steps. content: Ambassador Md. Daud Ali inaugurated the Bangladesh Pavilion at “Fashion World Tokyo (Autumn) 2026” at Tokyo Big Sight today by cutting a ribbon and visited the stalls. He praised the high quality of the Bangladeshi products on display and interacted with the participating entrepreneurs. A total of 25 Bangladeshi companies with 27 booths under the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB), along with 5 other renowned institutions, are participating in the fair. Following the inauguration, a seminar titled “Bangladesh: Sourcing Excellence for Apparel, Home Textile and Leather Products” was held at the exhibition hall of Tokyo Big Sight. Jointly organized by the Embassy of Bangladesh in Tokyo, EPB, and the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO), the seminar brought together business representatives and investors from both countries. Addressing the seminar as the chief guest, Ambassador Md. Daud Ali stated that Bangladesh is not merely a manufacturing country, but a reliable sourcing and investment partner for Japanese businesses. He highlighted the immense potential of Bangladesh’s robust production base across various sectors, including apparel, textiles, leather and footwear, pharmaceuticals, ceramics, agro-processing, and ITES. He further expressed optimism that the Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) will further strengthen bilateral trade and economic cooperation between the two nations. Mr. Yuji Ando, Senior Director for Global Strategy at JETRO, delivered a presentation highlighting the quality and competitive, reasonable pricing of Bangladesh’s apparel, home textiles, and leather products. summary: STONEVILLE, N.C. — October 8, 2026 — Reshoring Textiles has acquired Sans Technical Fibers, an American producer of high tenacity LDI nylon 6.6 and polyester yarns. Sans will operate alongside Spinnere as a sister company within Reshoring Textiles, and industry veteran John Garner has been named its CEO. Robert Antoshak has been named Chief Marketing […]
content: STONEVILLE, N.C. — October 8, 2026 — Reshoring Textiles has acquired Sans Technical Fibers, an American producer of high tenacity LDI nylon 6.6 and polyester yarns. Sans will operate alongside Spinnere as a sister company within Reshoring Textiles, and industry veteran John Garner has been named its CEO. Robert Antoshak has been named Chief Marketing Officer of Reshoring Textiles. The acquisition adds domestic filament production for technical and specialty uses, including sewing thread and industrial textiles, giving Reshoring more to offer manufacturers in apparel and industrial markets. “Reshoring is dedicated to helping American textile manufacturing grow,” said Josh Nieuwsma, CEO of Reshoring Textiles. “Customers need reliable long-term domestic sources of the raw materials their products require. Sans gives us an established operation with deep experience in specialty nylon and polyester. Alongside Spinnere, it will help us supply more of those needs from U.S. facilities, and support manufacturers and startups looking to grow and build their businesses here.” Based in Stoneville, North Carolina, Sans has supplied high tenacity filaments for more than two decades. Its nylon yarns range from ultrafine to heavier deniers and offer UV stabilization and favorable dyeing characteristics. The company expanded into polyester in 2017, with new production equipment entering service in 2018 and in 2024. Sans now offers polyester yarns from fine deniers to heavy denier industrial. With new extrusion equipment on its way, Sans will be able to offer significantly more and different polymers to its customers.
